inputs: Executed MSO service agreements or verified Arizona ABS licensing documents, state-specific ethics review, fixed/cost-plus rate cards, approved advertising materials, vendor contracts, and an allocation of clinical, legal, and administrative responsibilities.

Documented claimant permission, minimum necessary identifying data, authorized Lexis access and permitted-purpose verification, restricted SSN matching where justified, existing-client indexes, and secure duplicate-review procedures.

Valid patient access requests or medical-record authorizations, provider and EHR inventories, delivery instructions, applicable record-fee rules, privacy/security agreements where required, and a cost ledger for retrieval, processing, and human review.
operator_plays.mechanism: Operate a non-lawyer Management Services Organization furnishing fixed or documented cost-plus marketing, intake administration, duplicate-claimant screening, and medical-record retrieval, while the law firm retains client selection, legal advice, litigation judgment, and settlement control under applicable state versions of ABA Model Rule 5.4 and related advertising and solicitation rules. Alternatively, participate through an actually licensed Arizona Alternative Business Structure within its authorized scope, rather than assuming an Arizona license overrides restrictions in other jurisdictions; non-lawyer MSO compensation must not become impermissible legal-fee sharing or payment for recommendations. Retrieve electronic records under valid patient requests or authorizations and 45 CFR § 164.524 as applicable, distinguishing individual-access fee limits from third-party requests whose treatment differs under HITECH and subsequent case law; the collectible base is earned contractual service fees actually paid, not projected settlements, with record-copying, identity-verification, security, and professional-review costs separately accounted for.
metrics: Collected service economics: paid fixed/cost-plus invoices, receivables aging, and contribution after record charges, identity checks, licensed data access, security, and review labor.
Triage quality: confirmed duplicate rate, false-positive rate after human review, source-linked record completeness, and percentage of files requiring additional patient authorization.
Operational integrity: request-to-record turnaround, overdue access requests, unauthorized-access incidents, and compensation exceptions linked to referrals, settlements, or legal-fee percentages.
operator_plays.name: Rule 5.4-Aligned Law-Firm MSO and Patient-Directed Electronic-Records Triage Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of contracts with outcome-linked compensation, unauthorized legal-decision exceptions, jurisdictional licensing gaps, and record requests missing verified authority.
platform_risks.failure_mode: An administrative services arrangement drifts into prohibited fee sharing, paid recommendations, unauthorized legal practice, or unauthorized health-record access.
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend the affected activity, refer legal decisions to licensed counsel, correct pricing and marketing under ethics review, restrict improperly obtained records, and resume only services supported by valid contracts, permissions, and jurisdictional authority.
platform_risks.impact: The law firm and operator face disciplinary, licensing, privacy, contractual, and collection exposure, while affected records and invoices may require remediation.
platform_risks.trigger: Compensation becomes settlement-linked, marketing promises legal outcomes, staff make legal eligibility decisions, Arizona licensing is treated as nationwide permission, or records are requested without a valid authority pathway.

workflow: 1. Choose and document the operating structure with qualified ethics counsel: use a fixed/cost-plus MSO without prohibited ownership or fee sharing, or obtain the required Arizona ABS license before operating as one; review every jurisdiction served and preserve lawyers' independent judgment.

2. Run approved marketing and administrative intake without selling legal recommendations or making merits determinations; match permitted claimant identifiers against authorized internal and Lexis records, minimize SSN exposure, and send possible duplicates or conflicts to the firm's designated reviewer.

3. Submit properly scoped patient requests or authorizations and distinguish patient access from third-party disclosure pathways; apply the relevant fee rules and, for requests governed by § 164.524, track its 30-calendar-day response period and permitted single extension with written notice, while checking shorter applicable state deadlines.

4. Deduplicate and organize received records into source-linked timelines for lawyer review, restrict access and retention, and invoice documented fixed or cost-plus services independently of settlement size, legal fees, or outcome; reconcile service payments against actual delivery costs.

operator_plays.name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates
operator_plays.mechanism: Pairing an Arizona Alternative Business Structure (ABS) or co-counsel law firm with an institutional litigation-finance credit facility to acquire, medically verify (via $6.50 HITECH patient-directed record requests), and package 1,000–25,000 retained mass-tort plaintiffs (PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, defective medical devices) at $1,200–$2,500 CAC—either flipping vetted case tranches to litigation-finance hedge funds at 2.5x–4x cost or holding for 35–40% global MDL settlement fee splits.
inputs: Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (JPML) docket analytics, FDA FAERS adverse-event spikes, and EPA contaminant zip-code maps
Arizona ABS / co-counsel retainer infrastructure with e-sign intake and automated HITECH Act (45 CFR § 164.524) medical-record retrieval engine
Non-recourse litigation-finance warehouse credit facility and MDL leadership co-counsel placement contracts
workflow: Identify emerging MDL mass torts with clear causation biomarkers (specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes + geographic/product exposure proof) and deep-pocket corporate defendants
Run hyper-targeted CTV, paid social, and public-record outbound campaigns to sign injured claimants directly onto joint co-counsel retainer agreements

Execute automated HITECH patient-directed electronic medical record (EMR) pulls at the federal statutory cap (~$6.50/record) and use LLM clinical parsers to verify qualifying diagnosis and exposure dates within 72 hours

Securitize verified, deficiency-free case tranches into litigation-finance buyout facilities at $4,500–$9,000 per vetted retainer or hold on the balance sheet for $25,000–$80,000+ gross contingency fees at MDL settlement
metrics: All-in cost per medically verified, deficiency-free retained plaintiff ($1,200–$2,500)
HITECH medical-record retrieval turnaround time (hours) and clinical qualification pass rate (%)
Secondary docket tranche sale multiple (2.5x–4.0x CAC) or net MDL settlement IRR

platform_risks.failure_mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake
platform_risks.trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants
platform_risks.impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders

operator_plays.name: Arizona ABS Law-Firm Ownership & Survivor/Mass-Tort Co-Counsel Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Leverage Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1(c) and ACJA § 7-209 (which abolished ABA Rule 5.4 in Arizona via Alternative Business Structure [ABS] licensing) so non-lawyer acquisition operators can legally own an Arizona law firm, acquire inbound institutional sexual assault survivor claims (juvenile detention facilities, rideshare MDLs, clergy/boarding-school/medical lookback windows) and catastrophic mass torts, and participate in lawful co-counsel contingency fee splits ($50k–$400k+ per settled case) instead of capped flat marketing fees.
inputs: Arizona Supreme Court ABS license + designated Compliance Lawyer (ACJA § 7-209)
Trauma-informed inbound acquisition funnels for state sexual-assault lookback windows & federal MDLs
24/7 HIPAA-compliant survivor intake, facility/ride-receipt verification, & national trial co-counsel network
workflow: Form or partner with a licensed Arizona ABS law firm with an appointed Arizona-bar Compliance Lawyer to legally bridge digital acquisition and legal representation
Run empathetic, 100% inbound survivor-advocacy campaigns across open statutory lookback windows (juvenile detention centers, Uber/Lyft rideshare MDL 3084, institutional/youth-facility abuse)

Execute trauma-informed intake, verify facility/detention/rideshare records, and co-counsel with specialized trial litigators under Rule 1.5(e) joint-responsibility agreements to share in back-end settlement fees
metrics: Cost per signed & record-verified survivor retainer ($1,200–$3,500 media cost)
Facility/rideshare corroboration pass rate (%) & zero-fraud docket quality
Realized co-counsel contingency fee per settled case ($50,000–$400,000+ vs. $3k lead sale)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Cross-jurisdictional Rule 5.4 fee-splitting challenges, MDL claimant-fraud rejections, or 24–48 month settlement lockup
platform_risks.trigger: Splitting fees in non-ABS jurisdictions without genuine legal services/joint responsibility by ABS attorneys, accepting unverified lead-brokered retainers, or undercapitalizing multi-year MDL hold times
platform_risks.impact: Disallowance of co-counsel fee division in restrictive states, court dismissal of uncorroborated claims, or working-capital exhaustion before settlement payout
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% primary-record corroboration rate (detention/medical/ride logs) and state-by-state Rule 1.5(e)/5.4 ethics opinion sign-off
platform_risks.fallback: Ensure licensed ABS attorneys perform substantive legal intake/case-work or pair with an MSO (Management Services Organization) structure in restrictive states, enforce strict primary-document verification before filing, and blend fast-settling single-event injury cases with multi-year institutional dockets

inputs: Authorized inbound traffic sources, accurate ads and landing pages, versioned recipient-specific disclosures, TrustedForm or Jornaya evidence where applicable, suppression records and permitted recording notices.

Ringba or Retreaver configuration, documented buyer ping-post endpoints, buyer authorization or licensing checks, vertical-specific eligibility rules, capacities and payout terms including any 90–120-second duration threshold.
Traffic cost data, call-detail records, transfer and consent events, buyer acceptance receipts, duplicate identifiers, dispute reason codes and restricted-access retention settings.
operator_plays.mechanism: Use Ringba or Retreaver-supported routing and buyer integrations to auction qualified inbound calls through sub-second ping-post trees, earning the spread between accepted buyer payouts and traffic acquisition costs. Operate separate programs for ACA/Medicare, auto/home insurance, mass-tort legal intake and emergency home services, with recipient-specific consent where required, sector-specific transfer restrictions and privacy-minimized bid payloads. TrustedForm or Jornaya records can support evidence of the actual named-recipient disclosure but do not independently establish valid consent; negotiated 90–120-second duration triggers qualify payment only alongside genuine caller intent, buyer acceptance and applicable contract terms.
metrics: Net contribution per qualified call: collected buyer revenue minus acquisition, telephony, routing, verification and refund costs.
Routing quality: p95 auction latency, accepted-connection rate, abandonment rate and buyer capacity rejection rate by vertical.
Evidence and dispute quality: percentage of transfers with required recipient-specific permission records, duplicate rate, complaint rate and payout reversal rate.
operator_plays.name: Consent-Verified Inbound RTB Pay-Per-Call Exchange Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Consent-recipient mismatch count, complaint and reversal rates by source, and anomalous clustering of call endings immediately after the billing threshold.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A buyer or routing platform rejects calls or suspends the program because consent, marketing representations or traffic quality fails applicable requirements.
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected sources and transfers, preserve evidence securely, refund invalid billings and resume only with corrected disclosures, permitted compensation structures and verified buyer acceptance.
platform_risks.impact: Payout reversals, account suspension, consumer complaints and potential regulatory or contractual exposure.
platform_risks.trigger: Recipient mismatches, misleading ACA/Medicare advertising, restricted legal-referral fee structures, excessive duplicates or calls padded to cross a duration threshold.

workflow: 1. Approve legitimate traffic sources and buyer contracts, segregate verticals, and establish how each caller receives accurate recipient disclosures without misleading benefit claims or prohibited steering.

2. Screen intent, geography, duplicates and applicable transfer restrictions; obtain required permission before transmitting personal information and send only permitted minimal qualification metadata in bid requests.

3. Run the supported sub-second auction with timeouts and capacity checks, identify the selected recipient and obtain any required recipient-specific permission before transfer, then connect the caller without artificially extending duration.
4. Reconcile buyer acceptance and any 90–120-second billing condition against call records, resolve disputes, suppress invalid sources and settle only genuine, contract-qualified calls.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Fixed-Fee Mass-Tort MSO
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Build a four-person intake and administration pod around documented service costs, independent counsel, and collected invoices.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Experienced legal-operations managers serving plaintiff firms through fair-market fixed or cost-plus administrative service agreements.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 establish relevant telephone marketing requirements. State-adopted professional-conduct rules, including restrictions corresponding to ABA Model Rule 5.4, determine permitted MSO structures. The ABA model text is not itself a nationwide statute. Price administrative services independently of retainer signatures, legal fees, settlement awards, or litigation outcomes.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Evidence-Ready Record Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Turn authorized EMR and pharmacy requests into source-linked exposure chronologies, with clinical exceptions routed to qualified staff.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Medical-record operations specialists supporting mass-tort counsel with auditable retrieval, chronology preparation, and deficiency repair.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 45 CFR 164.524 governs individual access to protected health information, while 45 CFR 164.508 supplies authorization requirements for disclosures requiring authorization. The HHS Ciox notice limits how third-party directions and patient-rate fees may be characterized. 45 CFR 164.504(e) governs business-associate contracts where that relationship actually exists; a law-firm vendor is not automatically a business associate merely because it handles medical records.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Causation-Aware Intake Platform
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Separate claimant identity, usable proof, counsel acceptance, and vendor collections before expanding campaign exposure.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Plaintiff-firm operations leaders and separately licensed Arizona ABS operators building disciplined claimant acquisition infrastructure.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: Federal Rule of Evidence 702 makes expert reliability central to litigation risk; intake acceptance does not resolve general causation. Arizona's court-administered ABS licensing framework is a distinct ownership pathway, not a blanket exception available to an ordinary MSO or to operations in every jurisdiction.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46 ranks #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: a small-team administrative infrastructure business, not ownership of plaintiffs or settlement proceeds. This chapter maps 13 operator plays across fixed-fee MSOs, identity controls, patient-directed records, clinical chronology, licensed Arizona ABS structures, and a separately bounded CTV supply operation. The collectible product is documented service delivery under enforceable contracts. Annual owner profit is $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled, on respective service revenues of $160,000, $705,000, and $1,250,000. Durable operators reconcile every inquiry through proof and collection, preserve attorney judgment, distinguish access requests from third-party authorizations, and price replacement work before buying another lead.

sections.heading: 1. Sell an auditable administrative service, never a slice of litigation
paragraphs: Mass-tort case acquisition begins with attracting potential claimants, but the defensible business is a contracted operating system around a law firm's intake desk. The non-lawyer management services organization supplies campaign administration, scripted intake, document routing, identity checks, record retrieval, and evidence indexing. The law firm decides whom to represent, what legal theories to pursue, which deadlines control, and whether to settle. Those boundaries belong in the agreement, staff permissions, call scripts, and invoice descriptions. A service described as administrative becomes a different proposition when compensation follows settlement size or staff promise a claimant that a lawsuit qualifies. Applicable state versions of ABA Model Rule 5.4, solicitation restrictions, and unauthorized-practice rules control; the ABA model text itself is not a nationwide operating license. California Business and Professions Code sections 6151 and 6152 illustrate why a paid runner model cannot be repaired merely by renaming referral payments. Start with a documented fair-market monthly scope, defined capacity, and separately priced change orders. Preserve attorney supervision without letting the vendor choose legal outcomes. The first durable asset is a clean allocation of authority that a replacement employee can follow without interpreting litigation strategy.

The primary mapped play is aba_compliant_law_firm_mso_and_hitech_emr_triage, designated TRACK_1. Its unit is a service obligation: for example, an illustrative $10,000 monthly desk contract buys defined staffing coverage, secure routing, and a stated retrieval workload, rather than ten successful lawsuits. Twelve delivered months produce $120,000 of service billings before credits, collection losses, or principal-versus-agent adjustments. The same arrangement can use documented cost-plus pricing, such as $8,000 of eligible monthly costs plus a 25% markup, provided the result remains supportable and is not a disguised recommendation payment. Patient access and medical chronology are operational services, not diagnoses or legal sufficiency opinions. A licensed clinician handles clinical ambiguity where the engagement requires that expertise; counsel determines whether evidence supports representation. An actually licensed Arizona alternative business structure offers another ownership path under Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1 and ACJA section 7-209. That license does not export permission into every state. If the compensation design, marketing, or authority fails review, suspend the affected work, restrict improperly obtained records, route legal decisions to counsel, and resume only the services supported by corrected contracts, permissions, and jurisdictional authority.

For this chapter, the 13 mapped plays are an editorial operating map, not thirteen independently supplied scorecards: the core MSO play; duplicate-claimant screening; retainer administration; patient-access retrieval; pharmacy-proof retrieval; exposure chronology; deficiency remediation; attorney-advertising operations; CRM integration; service reporting; Arizona ABS administration; secure matter archiving; and the separately specified CTV supply play. The five archetypes below group these functions into businesses a small team can actually supervise. A founder should select one anchor contract and attach adjacent services only when the same evidence and permissions support them. Selling every function immediately creates incompatible turnaround promises and several distinct professional boundaries. The operational moat comes from provider-specific retrieval knowledge, reproducible identity matching, source-linked chronologies, and reliable replacement handling. It does not come from keeping claimants in a proprietary black box or making counsel dependent on inaccessible documents. Clients should receive exportable records and an intelligible audit trail. Price the cost of that portability into the service. Startup capital of $12,000–$50,000 funds initial systems, contract work, staffing deposits, and retrieval float; the expected first deal takes one to four months. Buying traffic before establishing these mechanics consumes capital without creating a usable operating asset.

callout.title: Build the evidence trail before expanding paid intake
callout.body: Experienced operators buy fewer ambiguous handoffs and make every administrative decision reproducible from source evidence.
items: Store the exact landing-page text and TrustedForm certificate reference together; a certificate without the actual disclosure cannot explain what the claimant saw.
Maintain a provider routing ledger separating medical records, billing records, imaging, and pharmacy fulfillment; one fax destination rarely serves every record category.
Use duplicate matches as review flags, not automatic accusations; twins, shared phones, changed surnames, and household addresses create legitimate collisions.
Negotiate a precise replacement window and evidence standard before launch; reserve expected rework costs when the original service is delivered.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile recognized service revenue to the conversion waterfall
paragraphs: Recognized operator revenue is earned flat or documented cost-plus MSO administrative, marketing, intake, and records-triage fees. It excludes law-firm trust funds, settlement awards, claimant recoveries, and the firm's own legal fees. Under ASC 606, identify the customer contract, promised services, transaction price, allocation, and when each obligation is satisfied. A stand-ready desk commonly recognizes service revenue over the covered period; a distinct completed records packet may follow a different delivery pattern. Cash received in advance is not automatically earned revenue, while an earned receivable is not cash available for payroll. Track accrual revenue and collected fees separately. Evaluate whether the MSO controls media or retrieval services before transfer: principal treatment can support gross presentation, while an agent generally recognizes its fee or retained share rather than reimbursed spend. The canonical cases already specify operator service revenue; do not multiply them by an invented retained_share or add client advertising budgets on top. If $20,000 of client media funds passes through an agency arrangement alongside a $3,000 earned administration fee, the operating revenue is $3,000, not $23,000. Record credits and constrained variable consideration consistently with the underlying contract.

Use the full waterfall: raw inquiry -> signed law-firm retainer -> usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof -> deficiency-free accepted case -> collected MSO/vendor fee. An illustrative monthly cohort starts with 1,000 inquiries at $20 each, costing $20,000. Duplicate screening removes 200, and counsel-directed intake converts 25% of the remaining 800 into 200 signed retainers. Records work costs $60 per signed file, or $12,000. Usable proof arrives for 140 files, and 100 ultimately satisfy counsel's documented acceptance criteria without outstanding deficiencies. Suppose a separate fixed-capacity contract earns $50,000 that month and the client pays $48,000 initially; the remaining $2,000 is a receivable, not additional collected revenue. Another $10,000 of labor and systems produces $42,000 of direct operating costs, leaving $8,000 before other overhead on the earned basis and $6,000 on the immediate cash basis. These are illustrative cohort economics, not a replacement scorecard. Dividing the fee by 100 accepted cases gives a diagnostic $500 service allocation per accepted file, not permission to charge for recommendations. If proof yield falls from 70% to 50%, only 100 files reach the proof stage, while the original retrieval outlay remains $12,000.

The canonical annual cases reconcile exactly: $160,000 less $118,400 of total expenses equals $41,600 owner net profit; $705,000 less $437,100 equals $267,900; and $1,250,000 less $625,000 equals $625,000. Their margins are respectively 26%, 38.0%, and 50%, with teams of one full-time employee plus three contractors, one plus three, and two plus four. These figures are the complete scenario envelope, not proof that any traffic channel can produce those results. The stated $2,500–$14,000 monthly operating-expense range is a planning input rather than a cap on all-in scenario costs; the annual totals also have to absorb variable delivery and acquisition expenses. An illustrative revenue bridge uses four $40,000 annual contracts for Conservative, five $141,000 contracts for Base, and ten $125,000 contracts for Scaled. Actual scopes must justify those prices. Stress the cohort again with 300 duplicates, 175 signed files, and $10,500 of retrieval costs at the same signing rate and unit cost. Add twenty replacement files at $60 each: another $1,200 leaves the business before any additional collection. Preserve a cash reserve for provider invoices, replacements, and client payment delays rather than treating uncollected invoices as available owner distributions.

sections.heading: 3. Choose a sub-vertical whose evidence and distribution economics survive scrutiny
paragraphs: The comparison matrix covers sixteen sub-verticals: the thirteen mapped plays and three supporting record categories. Its named platforms illustrate available rails, not confirmed integrations, vendor endorsements, or advertised prices. Each fee structure is a proposed operator contract design. The core MSO can coordinate retrieval, but pharmacy proof, implant identification, and occupational exposure require different evidence. A diagnosis code may support a chart search without proving ingestion, product identity, dose, or a legally relevant exposure window. A paid prescription can be reversed, an ordered medicine can remain unfilled, and a problem-list diagnosis can persist after a clinician changes their assessment. Demand source pages and event dates rather than treating extracted text as an established fact. Configure AWS Textract or another approved extraction service only after determining applicable privacy obligations, contractual protections, and access controls. An LLM chronology should attach every material assertion to a document identifier and page, preserve conflicting dates, and route uncertainty to a reviewer. Never let the model invent missing exposure history. The sellable advantage is a shorter, measurable path from authorized source collection to counsel review, with correction costs included in the quoted service capacity.

The second supplied play, ctv_mfa_programmatic_supply_arbitrage, is TRACK_2 and must remain economically separate from claimant processing. Its proposed fleet comprises 50–200 free utility, ambient, public-domain cinema, weather, or casual-gaming channels across Roku, Fire TV, Samsung Tizen, and mobile stores. The supplied thesis contrasts $0–$2 acquisition CPM with $18–$35 monetized video CPM. Those are planning inputs, not verified market quotes, and acquisition impressions are not interchangeable with billable ad impressions. Illustratively, $2,000 buys one million acquisition impressions at $2 CPM. If that cohort produces 200,000 valid monetized impressions at $25 CPM, gross receipts are $5,000; a 20% platform share leaves $4,000, or $2,000 before content, hosting, support, and reconciliation costs. At 50,000 monetized impressions, net receipts fall to $1,000 and acquisition alone loses $1,000. Track actual users, sessions, fill, invalid traffic, deductions, and payment timing. The fallback is genuine viewer check-ins, accurate app-ads.txt and supply-chain declarations, and diversification across six or more independent SSPs plus direct agency PMP deals where contracts permit. Stop rejected inventory rather than manufacturing engagement or concealing its source.

Do not finance a mass-tort desk by assuming that CTV inventory will clear premium agency demand. An ambient app is not automatically eligible for Fortune 500 budgets, and legitimate supply requires documented rights, truthful classification, and buyer acceptance. If the firm buys ads on operator-owned channels, disclose the relationship, benchmark the media price, and maintain separate media and administrative contracts. Health-related intake information must not become an audience export or a retargeting seed. For ordinary plaintiff acquisition, evaluate Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising, and permitted publisher placements against their current sensitive-category policies before spending. Attorney-advertising and solicitation requirements still apply even when a platform accepts the advertisement. Capture firm-specific contact permission as an operating standard, including the named caller, channels, purpose, disclosure version, timestamp, and withdrawal handling. The FCC's attempted one-to-one lead-generation consent rule was vacated in 2025; do not present that vacated amendment as current federal law. Existing TCPA restrictions, applicable written-consent requirements, do-not-call rules, and state requirements remain fact-specific constraints. A TrustedForm certificate supports provenance but does not establish that every later call is permitted. Suspend disputed sources and preserve the evidence needed to resolve both the vendor credit and contact restriction.

sections.heading: 4. Turn permissions, source evidence, and replacement handling into the moat
paragraphs: HITECH is not a universal command to send any law-firm request cheaply and immediately. Classify the request before submitting it. Individual access under 45 CFR section 164.524 concerns the designated record set and carries specific access, timing, form, and fee rules. Covered entities ordinarily must act within thirty days; one additional thirty-day extension requires a timely written explanation and completion date. Electronic production depends on the requested form being readily producible or another agreed readable electronic format. A HIPAA authorization under section 164.508 is a different instrument, and third-party-directed requests require attention to HITECH's electronic-health-record provision and the Ciox litigation's effect on HHS interpretation. Do not extend the individual-access fee limitation automatically to third-party transmission. Track request type, patient signature, recipient designation, record scope, requested format, submission evidence, provider response, and assessed charges. State requirements may add applicable rights or restrictions. Separate the provider's permissible copying charge from the MSO's contracted administrative work. When a provider disputes the request, correct the routing or authority rather than impersonating the patient or using their portal credentials. Escalate contested access and pricing questions through the appropriate documented process.

Determine each participant's HIPAA role from actual functions and relationships. A law firm holding claimant records is not automatically a covered entity, and every vendor handling health information is not automatically its business associate. Where business-associate status applies, execute the required agreements and flow obligations to qualifying subcontractors under 45 CFR sections 164.502(e) and 164.504(e). Apply appropriate access restrictions and security even when another privacy regime governs. Separate client workspaces, require multifactor authentication, log exports, and restrict raw identifiers to personnel with a defined task. Do not promise cross-firm duplicate-retainer detection without lawful access to the relevant data; no generic identity tool establishes every existing representation. Use verified claimant statements, permitted client records, and counsel-directed conflict processes. Keep extraction output distinct from reviewed chronology. Professional reviewers should sample both accepted and rejected files because false rejections silently destroy usable evidence. Set retention and deletion instructions by contract, applicable obligations, and preservation needs; an access termination must not erase material subject to a litigation hold. The operator's security moat is repeatable evidence custody, not a dashboard badge or an unsupported claim that a tool solves privacy.

Finally, underwrite litigation concentration as a service-continuity risk rather than a settlement forecast. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 requires the proponent to establish the rule's admissibility conditions more likely than not; adverse general-causation rulings can collapse demand across an MDL. That can strand advertising commitments and retrieval work even when every inquiry was genuine. Diversify contracted services and clients, limit advance media exposure, and specify what happens to work in progress when counsel pauses a campaign. Avoid promising replacement claimants after scientific or legal criteria change; distinguish vendor defects from a new litigation decision. Run a weekly ledger linking invoice lines to service periods, completed tasks, credits, provider charges, and actual collections. Review aging by client, record source, and delivery cohort so that slow payment cannot hide behind aggregate lead volume. Scale only after the desk repeatedly delivers its contracted scope without founder-only interventions. The six-person Scaled case requires narrow workflows, bounded exceptions, and credible contractor capacity, not unlimited automation. If authority, evidence provenance, or compensation fails, stop that activity, preserve the audit trail, correct the defect, and restart the lawful service rather than buying more volume.

callout.title: Four pre-flight verifications before accepting live intake
callout.body: Proceed only when the desk can demonstrate its authority, source permissions, operational readiness, and cash coverage.
items: Verify the executed MSO agreement uses supportable fixed or documented cost-plus compensation and expressly reserves representation, legal advice, and settlement decisions to authorized lawyers.
Verify each acquisition source preserves the actual disclosure, firm-specific contact permission, suppression process, and applicable attorney-advertising requirements.
Verify records-request classification, valid patient authority, recipient details, applicable privacy contracts, and tested tenant-separated storage before receiving live records.
Verify the budget funds retrieval outlays and contracted replacements through the expected collection delay; exclude projected settlement receipts from available cash.

sop_steps.action: Execute a jurisdiction-reviewed administrative scope with measurable capacity.
sop_steps.detail: List excluded legal decisions, eligible cost-plus inputs, replacement terms, change-order pricing, and invoice evidence.

sop_steps.title: Establish the authorized claimant record
sop_steps.action: Capture provenance, resolve identity exceptions, and route retainer decisions to the firm.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve contact permissions and duplicate-review rationale; do not infer representation from an advertising inquiry.

sop_steps.title: Retrieve and review source-linked proof
sop_steps.action: Submit correctly classified requests and build a cited chronology.
sop_steps.detail: Record provider charges and response dates, distinguish filled prescriptions from orders, and escalate clinical ambiguity.

sop_steps.title: Close the service and collection loop
sop_steps.action: Reconcile delivered obligations, client deficiencies, credits, and actual payments.
sop_steps.detail: Update the full conversion waterfall, fund outstanding replacement exposure, and recognize revenue under the contract's performance obligations rather than projected case value.

chapters.pull_quote: Own the reliability of the service desk, not a fictional share of the claimant's recovery.
action_checklist: Select one of the five operator archetypes and write a fixed-capacity scope that reserves all legal decisions to the law firm.
Build the inquiry-to-collected-fee waterfall with separate duplicate, proof-rejection, deficiency, replacement, and payment-aging fields.
Reconcile the three canonical scenarios to $41,600, $267,900, and $625,000 annual owner net profit without adding settlements or client pass-through funds.
Create a provider routing ledger that separates individual-access requests, third-party directions, and authorizations with their applicable fee treatment.
Test source-linked chronology review, tenant-separated access, export logging, and incident handling using synthetic records before live operation.
Keep the CTV operation on a separate ledger and stop any inventory whose genuine engagement, declared provenance, or buyer eligibility cannot be demonstrated.

chapters.title: Who Pays, Why They Pay & How the Payment Rail Works
chapters.subtitle: Law-Firm Operating Budgets, HIPAA Access Requests, Rule 5.4 Boundaries, and Collectible Fixed-Fee MSO Contracts
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46 ranks #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score and 13 mapped plays. Its dependable customer is the law firm buying documented administrative capacity, not the claimant awaiting a settlement. Managing partners authorize budgets; finance teams release operating cash; docket leaders validate deliverables. Separate those roles before purchasing media or requesting records. Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits are $41,600, $267,900, and $625,000 on contracted MSO revenue of $160,000, $705,000, and $1,250,000. This chapter connects intake conversion, medical-proof rejection, fixed-fee acceptance, and eight payment rails. It also distinguishes licensed litigation-finance structures from ordinary nonlawyer vendors, corrects the universal $6.50 retrieval assumption, and makes customer credit quality part of every acquisition decision.

sections.heading: 1. Sell Budget Certainty to the Person Who Can Release Operating Cash
paragraphs: The economic buyer is usually a managing partner, practice-group leader, or chief operating officer who has committed payroll and advertising cash before knowing which inquiries become supportable claims. The acute pain is stranded acquisition expense: duplicate retainers, missing exposure evidence, unreachable patients, and staff repeatedly opening the same incomplete file. Sell a measurable administrative service that removes those costs, rather than a promise of settlement value. The budget owner wants predictable monthly capacity; the intake director wants fewer rework loops; the controller wants an invoice that matches a purchase order. Ask each person what evidence permits payment, who can reject work, and whose signature changes scope. A partner's enthusiasm is insufficient when accounts payable requires vendor onboarding, tax documentation, and a separate banking review. Document the contracting entity, authorized signer, billing address, purchase-order reference, and operating-account payer before launch. For an illustrative $30,000 pilot, require a $15,000 advance credited against services and a $15,000 invoice after the agreed processing period. Record the advance as a contract liability until earned. The advance purchases capacity; it does not buy ownership of a claimant, a legal retainer, or settlement proceeds.

Budget authority and custody authority are different permissions. A firm's finance lead may approve vendor expenses without authority to release client trust money, while a settlement administrator may control distributions without purchasing your services. Make the ordinary payment source the firm's operating account. If a litigation funder supplies working capital, the borrower remains the invoice obligor unless a separate enforceable payment undertaking says otherwise. A funder's presentation, term sheet, or conditional commitment is not cash available for payroll. Inspect executed facility conditions, borrowing availability, concentration limits, and permitted uses with the firm's authorized finance team. Never seek claimant-level privileged material merely to perform credit screening; aggregate balances and redacted financial evidence normally answer the commercial question. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model rule, so identify the jurisdiction's adopted version and applicable exceptions instead of treating its text as a nationwide statute. Fair-market fixed or cost-plus pricing helps separate administrative compensation from legal fees, but pricing alone does not cure paid recommendations, prohibited solicitation, or interference with professional judgment. The supervising lawyer must retain decisions about representation, legal eligibility, case strategy, and client communications requiring legal judgment. Your contract should identify those reserved decisions explicitly.

Reconcile the commercial story to Formula v2.0 before discussing scale. Conservative annual revenue of $160,000 supports $118,400 of total modeled costs and $41,600 owner profit at 26%. Base revenue of $705,000 supports $437,100 of costs and $267,900 profit at 38.0%. Scaled revenue of $1,250,000 supports $625,000 of costs and $625,000 profit at 50%. Staffing remains 1 FT plus 3 contractors in the first two cases and 2 FT plus 4 contractors at scale. One illustrative Base billing mix is five firms purchasing $8,000 monthly capacity, producing $480,000 annually, plus fifteen separately scoped $15,000 projects producing $225,000. That mix explains revenue, not an automatic cost outcome; labor, software, insurance, retrieval, and collection expense must still fit the $437,100 envelope. Do not add merchant advertising volume, a funder's loan principal, gross settlements, or lawyer contingency fees to these numbers. Apply ASC 606 principal-agent analysis separately to pass-through purchases; no retained-share multiplier is supplied for this scorecard. Startup capital of $12,000–$50,000 and monthly operating expense of $2,500–$14,000 describe launch planning, not a substitute for complete annual scenario costs. Cash advances improve liquidity without increasing recognized revenue before performance.

callout.title: Make the Controller Comfortable Before the Partner Becomes Enthusiastic
callout.body: Veteran operators sell a short, auditable path from approved capacity to payable invoice, while leaving representation and legal fees with the authorized legal practice.
items: Send a specimen invoice, purchase-order template, and acceptance report during procurement; discover billing defects before the first service period.
Ask accounts payable to identify its payment cutoff and bank-release days; schedule acceptance early enough to avoid an accidental extra billing cycle.
Price records-location research separately from successful retrieval so provider silence does not turn unlimited follow-up into unpaid work.
Require a dated rejection code and source reference for replacement requests; freeze the applicable intake checklist for each purchased service period.

sections.heading: 2. Price the Entire Inquiry-to-Cash Waterfall, Including Failed Medical Proof
paragraphs: Track the full conversion waterfall as separate events: raw inquiry, signed law-firm retainer, usable HITECH EMR or pharmacy proof, deficiency-free accepted case, and collected MSO or vendor fee. An illustrative cohort begins with 1,000 raw inquiries and removes 120 duplicate or suspect submissions, leaving 880 for processing. Of those, 220 sign retainers, a 25% conversion among screened inquiries. Medical proof supports 154, reflecting 30% nonqualifying or unusable records among signed matters. Sixteen additional files retain unresolved deficiencies, leaving 138 accepted cases. If collections reporting links 124 accepted files to paid service periods, fourteen remain associated with unpaid periods; this is an attribution metric, not a per-case fee entitlement. Separately, a $30,000 fixed pilot invoice with $27,000 collected and $3,000 contractually held has a 90% cash realization rate. Never multiply accepted cases by an invented contingency share. Client-direct media of $12,000 represents $12 per raw inquiry, $54.55 per signed retainer, and $86.96 per accepted case before other costs. These are illustrative administrative funnel economics, not the mandated annual scorecard and not the much higher all-in acquisition costs assumed by the litigation-finance play. Keep the denominators visible in every buyer report.

Do not advertise $6.50 as the universal price of a lawyer-directed medical-record request. Under 45 CFR 164.524, covered entities may use an optional flat fee of no more than $6.50 for certain electronic copies supplied through the individual's access right; it is one permitted fee method, not a universal cap on every request. The Ciox decision and subsequent HHS guidance distinguish third-party directives from requests delivering records to the individual. A HIPAA authorization under 45 CFR 164.508 is also not interchangeable with an access request. Record the actual request pathway, recipient, requested format, provider, and quoted fee before committing retrieval expense. For illustration, 220 qualifying requests at an elected $6.50 flat fee cost $1,430; a $25 average instead costs $5,500, a $4,070 increase. Additional providers and pharmacy custodians create additional requests, so count requests rather than claimants. Section 164.524 generally allows thirty days, with one additional thirty-day extension supported by timely written explanation. Shorter applicable state requirements require separate tracking. Do not promise seven-day evidence delivery when provider response timing remains outside your control. Escalate overdue requests, preserve delivery receipts, and let the contract distinguish completed administrative work from unresolved provider production.

Treat fraud screening and clinical triage as evidence assembly, not automated representation decisions. TrustedForm can preserve lead-source and interaction evidence; it cannot establish medical eligibility or prove every element of valid calling consent. LexisNexis identity tools may support permitted identity checks, but no vendor search establishes a universal duplicate-retainer registry. Combine permitted identifiers, claimant attestations, firm-conflict procedures, and documented human review. Minimize SSN collection and restrict access to any necessary identifiers. An LLM chronology parser should extract dates, ICD-10 references, medications, and exposure statements with page citations, then route contradictions to trained reviewers. A diagnosis code does not establish product exposure or legal causation. Where the relationship creates business-associate obligations, execute the required agreement and apply minimum-necessary access, encryption, and retention controls. Define a thirty-day illustrative replacement window for objectively defective administrative deliverables, excluding later changes in litigation strategy or general-causation rulings under Federal Rule of Evidence 702. Reserve service credits against genuine vendor defects, not every unsuccessful claim. For calling campaigns, preserve seller-specific permission as an operating standard while applying current TCPA requirements; the FCC's attempted federal one-to-one consent rule was vacated in 2025. Review state calling restrictions separately rather than presenting that vacated rule as binding nationwide.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Spending Against a New Firm's Docket
callout.body: These checks determine whether the proposed service can be performed, billed, and collected within the agreed scope.
items: Verify the firm's legal entity, current professional status, authorized signer, operating-account payer, and documented ability to fund the first service period.

sections.heading: 3. Choose a Payment Rail That Matches the Obligor and the Funds
paragraphs: A payment rail moves money; it does not establish entitlement to money. Select the rail only after identifying the obligor, earned amount, source account, release conditions, and reconciliation owner. Wire transfers suit larger advances when bank instructions have been verified through an independently sourced callback. Domestic commercial wires can provide rapid availability, but fraud recovery is difficult and finality depends on the applicable system and law. ACH credits suit repeat operating invoices; ACH debits require appropriate authorization and monitoring for returns. Do not treat an initiated ACH entry as irrevocably collected cash. Record invoice identifiers in remittance fields, reconcile deposits daily, and investigate payer-name mismatches before crediting balances. An illustrative $20,000 invoice carrying a $25 wire charge yields $19,975 cash if the vendor absorbs that charge; contractually allocate charges instead of discovering the shortfall after payroll. Dual verification of changed bank details is more valuable than an elaborate dashboard that accepts emailed substitutions. Separate the person editing vendor bank instructions from the person authorizing releases. Require a new callback for every changed destination, even when the email appears inside an authentic prior thread. Preserve bank confirmation and remittance evidence with the invoice.

Escrow, advances, statutory disbursement, and milestone holds are commercial or custody arrangements rather than interchangeable bank networks. A neutral commercial escrow may release an MSO project payment upon specified administrative evidence, but its terms must identify whose money is held, permitted investments, dispute procedures, and fees. Do not relabel lawyer trust funds as commercial escrow to bypass professional rules. A vendor capacity retainer is an advance against administrative services, distinct from a client's legal retainer; its refund and earning terms belong in the service agreement. Statutory or court-supervised disbursements follow their own priorities, including applicable Medicare recovery obligations under 42 U.S.C. 1395y(b)(2). They are not an ordinary mechanism for paying unrelated MSO invoices. Platform checkout can simplify small purchases, yet processor underwriting, reserves, chargebacks, and restricted-business terms can interrupt availability. Use a truthful business description and obtain processor acceptance for the actual services sold. A 10% hold on a $30,000 project ties up $3,000; specify release after ten business days following documented acceptance, rather than after an indefinite future settlement. Every hold needs a finite trigger and an identified person authorized to confirm it. Otherwise the apparent receivable is an unsecured option granted to the customer.

Protect fees with documentation that survives staff turnover and disagreement. The master services agreement should define administrative deliverables, fair-market pricing support, authorized change orders, acceptance timing, correction obligations, invoice disputes, suspension rights, and governing law. A narrow noncircumvention clause can protect confidential vendor introductions and administrative work product where enforceable; it cannot give a nonlawyer ownership of clients or restrict client choice. Invoice accepted work even when a firm later changes its litigation thesis. Permit prompt payment of undisputed amounts while identified defects are resolved. Factoring may convert an earned MSO receivable into earlier cash, but distinguish that receivable from legal fees, claimant recoveries, and contingent settlement rights. For a $100,000 eligible invoice, an illustrative 85% advance provides $85,000 initially. If the debtor pays in full and total agreed fees equal $3,000, a $12,000 reserve release produces $97,000 total proceeds before other charges. Check recourse, dilution, notification, assignment restrictions, and applicable enacted UCC Article 9 provisions. Never send patient charts to a factor merely to verify an invoice. Provide redacted acceptance evidence and obtain proper authorization for any necessary disclosures. Financing accelerates collection timing; it does not improve the underlying customer's obligation or erase disputes.

sections.heading: 4. Underwrite the Counterparty Before Scaling Financed Dockets or Advertising Spend
paragraphs: The mapped play litigation_finance_mass_tort_docket_securitization requires separation between licensed legal economics and vendor economics. Its proposed 1,000–25,000 retained plaintiffs at $1,200–$2,500 acquisition cost imply $1.2 million to $62.5 million of acquisition capital before financing and ongoing case expense. At the low endpoint, a proposed 2.5x–4x valuation on $1.2 million means $3 million–$4.8 million, but neither a buyer nor a lawful transferable asset follows from that arithmetic. Claimants are not inventory that an MSO can sell. Any financing, portfolio interest transfer, or co-counsel arrangement requires an authorized legal structure, client-rights analysis, professional independence, and applicable lawyer fee-division requirements. A proposed 35–40% settlement contingency describes legal compensation under valid representation arrangements, not ordinary MSO revenue or an automatic co-counsel allocation. Arizona ABS licensing is entity-specific and does not export permission to every jurisdiction. Verify the Supreme Court's licensing record and actual scope before committing capital. The ordinary MSO earns its agreed administrative fees whether the supported docket concerns PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, or medical devices. Do not embed the play's speculative portfolio multiples in the $705,000 Base revenue case or imply every named docket remains open, viable, or fundable.

Apply the play's fallback as a funded risk-management plan, not a slogan. Six to ten genuinely differentiated tort or commercial-casualty exposures can reduce concentration, but shared causation theories, judges, experts, and funders can make apparently separate dockets highly correlated. A Federal Rule of Evidence 702 general-causation exclusion may impair many matters simultaneously. Model a complete freeze of the largest docket and thirty additional days of unpaid administrative invoices. Offloading 50% of a $1.2 million tranche cost basis means recovering $600,000 through an executed, permitted financing or transfer arrangement; assume zero recovery until conditions are satisfied and cash clears. The instruction to pay media vendors only on EMR-verified retainers also needs translation into lawful procurement. Verify service quality against medical evidence where authorized, but do not mechanically adopt per-retainer compensation if local rules prohibit paid recommendations or solicitation. Use fixed-capacity or cost-plus contracts, documented defect credits, and short purchase periods instead. Screen the firm through professional-license records, entity registries, trade references, authorized financial statements, and relevant public litigation records. Confirm unrestricted operating liquidity rather than counting client trust balances. Require prefunding when the firm cannot demonstrate an independent source of payment.

The second mapped play, agency_ad_spend_card_multiplier_rebate_cycling, monetizes genuine authorized advertising purchases only when issuer, platform, and client contracts permit the arrangement. For an illustrative $100,000 monthly media purchase, a 2% eligible cash-equivalent reward creates $2,000 before costs. Subtract $600 financing expense, $400 processing expense, and a $700 contractually owed client rebate: only $300 remains before operational overhead and taxes. A $2,500 reserve or unexpected interest charge overwhelms that spread. Count points at a supportable redemption value, observe caps and exclusions, and never describe manufactured transactions as client media. The $100,000 advertising volume is not automatically MSO revenue; document the principal-agent conclusion and reward accounting separately from the scorecard. Obtain written spending limits, authorized platform access, beneficiary ownership, and reimbursement timing. Prohibit rewards-driven spending beyond the approved campaign budget. A practical exposure limit includes unpaid invoices, committed contractor work, unreimbursed media, and retrieval obligations, less cleared advances. Review that total weekly against the customer's approved credit ceiling. If reimbursement slips or reward eligibility changes, move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms immediately. Pause new purchases without blocking the firm's access to its existing campaign records, claimant files, or required transition materials.

chapters.question_prompt: What are the real unit economics, gross-to-net margin deductions, scrub/reversal reserves, and working-capital float requirements for mass-tort case acquisition, hitech record triage & law-firm msos?
chapters.title: Unit Economics, Margin Waterfall & Working-Capital Float
chapters.subtitle: Fixed-Fee MSO Cohorts, HIPAA Access Costs, Arizona ABS Boundaries, and the Cash Cost of Replacement Windows
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46 ranks #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 13 mapped plays. Its economic engine is contracted administrative, marketing, intake, and medical-record triage work, not settlement ownership disguised as vendor compensation. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. This chapter reconstructs those outcomes through acquisition spend, delivery labor, retrieval costs, replacement reserves, and collection timing. A Base cohort produces $58,750 in monthly service revenue and $22,325 in modeled owner profit, yet a 75-day funding interval consumes $91,062.50 before startup expenditure and liquidity protection. Arizona ABS contingency economics and web subscription checkout economics remain separately labeled comparisons, never silent additions to the MSO scorecard.

sections.heading: 1. Price the administrative service, then reconcile every dollar
paragraphs: Start with the revenue boundary, because a profitable spreadsheet can conceal an impermissible contract. The scorecard measures contracted flat or cost-plus MSO administrative, marketing, intake, and record-triage fees. It excludes settlement awards, client trust balances, loan principal, and the law firm's contingency receivable. Use a written statement of work defining staffing capacity, retrieval tasks, quality standards, invoice dates, and reasonable replacement obligations. Document fair-market pricing through comparable vendor quotations and time studies, rather than a percentage of legal fees or a payment for recommending counsel. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model framework; each applicable jurisdiction's adopted rules determine the enforceable restrictions. Marketing and solicitation restrictions also matter even when compensation is fixed. For this illustrative reconstruction, recognized annual service revenue equals gross service billings because there are no modeled pass-through collections or price concessions. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 before adopting that treatment in actual accounts. If the operator merely arranges third-party retrieval, recognize its net contractual compensation where agent treatment applies, not the entire reimbursement. No additional retained_share haircut applies to these canonical service-revenue figures; they already exclude the underlying legal recovery.

The annual waterfall below assigns explicit costs to the three supplied outcomes without changing their revenue or profit. Conservative expenses total $118,400; Base expenses total $437,100; Scaled expenses total $625,000. Subtracting those amounts from $160,000, $705,000, and $1,250,000 produces $41,600, $267,900, and $625,000 respectively. These cost allocations are planning assumptions, not additional facts supplied by the scorecard. Delivery labor includes contractor execution, supervision, and applicable employee payroll burden. The first full-time position is the working owner, whose residual compensation is the displayed owner profit; the Scaled labor budget also accommodates the second full-time employee. Contractor counts describe three or four fractional specialists, not guaranteed full-time equivalents. Convert dollars into purchased hours before promising service levels: Base delivery labor of $132,000 buys 3,300 annual hours at a blended loaded $40 rate. That supports 275 hours monthly across intake, retrieval coordination, and chronology quality control. Technology covers licensed systems and secure processing, while overhead covers insurance, accounting, and operating administration. Owner profit is before the owner's personal taxes. The model includes no borrowing expense; actual financing costs reduce the residual dollar for dollar.

Treat the four-percent reserve as a budget for expected replacement delivery work, not a device for protecting inflated revenue. Conservative reserves are $6,400, Base reserves $28,200, and Scaled reserves $50,000. Within the Base monthly cohort, $2,350 funds incremental recontact, corrective retrieval, and deficiency repair beyond the routine labor and retrieval budgets. At $100 per repair, that supports 23.5 repairs monthly. Track the incremental tasks separately so the same contractor hour never lands in both ordinary delivery expense and reserve utilization. A planning reserve does not automatically qualify as an accounting provision: the controller determines recognition and classification from the actual obligation. If the customer receives a price credit instead, evaluate variable consideration and reduce recognized revenue when appropriate; do not label that credit a replacement expense merely to preserve the headline. Uncollectible balances require a separate credit-loss assessment. Record disputes by cause, vendor, originating cohort, and deadline. A late duplicate discovered during a replacement window belongs to its original cohort's economic history, even when cash leaves next quarter. This preserves an honest comparison between acquisition sources and prevents new invoices from masking old delivery failures.

callout.title: Separate profitable cohorts from flattering invoices
callout.body: Keep operational attribution detailed while preserving fixed or cost-plus compensation that reflects actual services.
items: Tag every replacement hour with the original cohort and defect code; do not bury yesterday's duplicate claims in today's routine labor.
Obtain vendor quotations before agreeing to a fixed retrieval allowance; distinguish patient-access charges from authorized third-party production charges.
Export invoice, credit, and receipt identifiers from QuickBooks into the cohort ledger so a disputed invoice cannot appear as collected cash.
Measure contractor minutes per verified document and accepted chronology, then compare purchased hours with the actual three-contractor capacity.

sections.heading: 2. Follow the claimant funnel without turning it into a referral tariff
paragraphs: Use the complete conversion waterfall: raw inquiry to signed law-firm retainer to usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof to deficiency-free accepted case to collected MSO/vendor fee. Insert a duplicate and identity screen before spending on records. The illustrative Base month begins with 1,000 inquiries purchased through $15,000 of media, producing 200 signed retainers. Twenty duplicate or identity-deficient records are removed, leaving 180 retrieval attempts. Usable evidence emerges for 140 matters, and 120 survive the law firm's document and factual deficiency check. A retainer is a lawyer-client engagement, not evidence that exposure, injury, causation, venue, or limitations requirements are satisfied. TrustedForm certificates can help preserve the advertisement and permission trail; they do not establish claimant identity or adjudicate duplicate representation. Use appropriately permitted LexisNexis identity services alongside source-document checks and lawyer-directed conflict procedures. Tokenize identifiers, limit access, and resolve disputed matches through human review. A shared household phone number is not sufficient evidence of fraud. Collect only necessary identifiers and avoid sending medical narratives into advertising audiences. Preserve respectful, trauma-aware contact practices for survivors rather than increasing contact frequency to hit a conversion target.

The Base cohort's acquisition arithmetic is $15 per inquiry, $75 per signed retainer, $107.14 per evidence-supported matter, and $125 per deficiency-free accepted matter. These are internal cost ratios, not prices charged for recommending a lawyer. Monthly contracted revenue is $58,750; dividing by 120 accepted matters yields $489.58 of attributed service revenue per accepted matter. The contract still pays for specified services and capacity, rather than legal recovery or referral success. Routine retrieval spending of $3,000 across 180 attempts implies $16.67 per attempt as a blended planning assumption. Actual retrieval charges vary with request route, custodian, format, scope, and state rules. Under 45 CFR 164.524, patient-access requests have defined response duties and fee limitations; do not assume every authorization-based third-party request inherits the same fee treatment. The Ciox litigation narrowed parts of the third-party directive framework. Track the request's legal basis and verify the applicable rule before estimating cost or promising timing. A request under 45 CFR 164.508 and a patient-access request are not interchangeable simply because both retrieve records. Escalate an incorrect fee through the proper route without misrepresenting the requester's status.

Evidence quality is an economic control, not merely a clinical annotation. Build the chronology around dated source pages, provider identity, medication dispensing, exposure facts, and the firm's written intake criteria. An LLM can extract candidate ICD-10 codes and timeline events, but each material fact needs a retrievable source reference and a human check. An ICD-10 code alone does not establish product exposure or legal causation. Configure contractual confidentiality, appropriate business associate arrangements when applicable, access controls, and retention rules before processing protected health information. Measure false-positive extraction rates on sampled files and count correction time inside delivery costs. If usable proof falls from 140 to 122 matters while downstream acceptance remains 120/140, expected accepted output becomes 104.57 matters. Acquisition cost per accepted matter rises from $125 to $143.44. That deterioration first threatens delivery capacity, replacement expense, and renewals; it does not automatically erase fixed-fee revenue already earned. Define replacement deadlines and objective defect categories before launch. A general-causation exclusion under Federal Rule of Evidence 702 can damage an entire docket, so stop incremental acquisition when counsel withdraws the governing criteria instead of manufacturing medical support for unusable files.

callout.title: Verify four conditions before funding another cohort
callout.body: The operations lead and responsible lawyer confirm the service boundary and evidence requirements before additional spend.
items: Confirm the governing state's fee-sharing, advertising, and solicitation restrictions; retain the fair-market pricing support for the actual MSO service scope.

Verify the named seller's contact permission, channel, disclosure text, and revocation handling; treat one-to-one permission as an operating standard, not an assertion that the vacated FCC rule remains effective.
Test identity matching and duplicate escalation on representative files, with restricted identifier access and a documented human correction path.
Confirm the correct record-request authority, source-page evidence standard, replacement deadline, and invoice dispute procedure before promising delivery.

sections.heading: 3. Finance the service interval, not the hoped-for settlement
paragraphs: Profit is measured over an accounting period; survival depends on the cash calendar. Base monthly expenses are $36,425, including the replacement budget, against $58,750 of monthly earned fees. For a conservative funding approximation, assume those expenses must be financed throughout a 30-day contractual replacement hold followed by 45 days from invoice issuance to collection. The intervals are sequential in this example, creating 75 days of operating float; do not add them if the actual contract runs them concurrently. Using a 30-day planning month, the cash requirement is $36,425 multiplied by 75/30, or $91,062.50. This is a cost-carry approximation, not a claim that receivables equal that amount. Earned-fee receivables and unbilled contract assets depend on performance, invoicing, and revenue recognition. Build a weekly cash schedule with media debits, contractor payment dates, retrieval charges, taxes, and expected receipts. Contractor net-15 terms may reduce the peak, while advance media funding may increase it. Treat the approximation as a deliberately conservative starting point, then replace it with the actual timing of each cash line. Never use a client's trust funds to bridge the operator's working-capital deficit.

The advertised $12,000–$50,000 startup range and $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex range do not establish sufficient cash for these fully loaded cohorts. Their scope must be reconciled against acquisition, contractor delivery, retrieval, replacement costs, and collection timing; they cannot replace the complete expense waterfall. In the Base illustration, $25,000 of startup expenditure plus $91,062.50 of operating float and a $10,000 liquidity cushion requires $126,062.50 in initial funding. A $30,000 customer advance reduces external funding to $96,062.50, assuming the advance is available for contracted services and no refund restriction prevents its use. Receipt does not itself create earned revenue; account for the advance against performance obligations. Negotiate shorter invoicing intervals, transparent defect notices, and undisputed-amount payment rather than demanding an open-ended hold on the entire cohort. If five percent of a Base monthly invoice remains disputed, $2,937.50 is temporarily unavailable even when the other $55,812.50 arrives. Place that amount in the weekly cash schedule. Distinguish a delayed payment from a permanent concession and a disputed service from a genuinely uncollectible customer. Each has a different accounting treatment and a different operational remedy.

Separate the mapped play arizona_abs_mass_tort_cocounsel from the ordinary MSO ledger. Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1(c), ACJA Section 7-209, and the state's ABS licensing framework permit qualifying licensed structures with nonlawyer ownership; Arizona's removal of its Rule 5.4 prohibition does not repeal restrictions elsewhere. Licensing, authorized legal practice, lawyer independence, and applicable co-counsel requirements remain essential. Consider a separately modeled $100,000 collected legal fee, within the play's $50,000–$400,000-plus fee range, with a lawful, documented 40% allocation to the licensed ABS. Its $40,000 receipt less $8,000 acquisition, $4,000 evidence development, and $10,000 attorney work leaves $18,000 before overhead and financing. The amount is a legal-fee example, not the client's settlement and not incremental scorecard revenue. Institutional survivor claims involving detention facilities, clergy, schools, medical settings, or rideshare litigation require jurisdiction-specific limitation and lookback analysis plus primary-document verification before filing. A 24-month delay locks up the $22,000 outlay without interim reimbursement. Require substantive licensed attorney work, use separate fixed-fee MSO arrangements where appropriate in restrictive states, and blend suitable faster single-event matters with long dockets only when counsel independently supports acceptance.

sections.heading: 4. Stress the margin before expanding the acquisition budget
paragraphs: Run sensitivities against individual cost lines before combining adverse events. A twenty-percent acquisition increase reduces annual profit to $33,600 Conservative, $231,900 Base, and $575,000 Scaled, assuming unchanged service revenue and delivery output. A fifteen-percent routine labor increase produces $35,600, $248,100, and $595,000 respectively. Doubling the replacement allocation from four to eight percent of revenue produces $35,200, $239,700, and $575,000. These are stress outcomes, not replacements for the canonical scorecard. Combine all three shocks and residual profit becomes $21,200, $183,900, and $495,000. A thirty-day payment delay initially changes funding, not operating profit, unless it also generates financing expense or credit loss. At a simple twelve-percent annual borrowing rate, financing the additional Base $36,425 for ninety days costs $1,092.75 using a 360-day convention. State that convention instead of silently mixing day-count methods. Test customer concentration separately: losing a firm representing thirty percent of Base revenue removes $211,500 of annual revenue before any avoidable costs are released. Contractor flexibility helps only when notice terms and delivery commitments actually permit reductions. Pause fresh media before attempting to solve that shortfall through higher-volume borrowing.

The mapped play web2app_quiz_subscription_billing_bypass is an adjacent checkout comparison, not a method for monetizing survivor records. Model a separate consumer product with fifty subscribers paying $20 monthly through a transparent web quiz and permitted external checkout. Gross subscription billings are $1,000. At an assumed processor rate of 3% plus $0.30 per transaction, payment costs are $45. Deduct $600 of acquisition spending and $100 of monthly service costs to leave $255 before other overhead, taxes, refunds, and chargebacks. With identical acquisition and service costs, a fifteen-percent store fee leaves $150, while a thirty-percent fee leaves zero. Those comparisons exclude any additional external-purchase platform charges, which must be added where applicable. The resulting $105 or $255 difference is not a universal saving: regional rules, entitlements, subscription programs, taxes, and refund obligations determine the actual economics. Use approved in-app billing where required, with clear renewal pricing and straightforward cancellation. Do not place protected medical facts in quiz analytics or condition legal intake on purchasing a subscription. Maintain a separate ledger so this illustrative product contributes nothing to the MSO revenue and margin reconciliation.

Expansion requires both reproducible service quality and funded collection timing. Review acquisition cost per usable proof, accepted-file throughput, replacement utilization, disputed balances, and cash collection by originating month. A cheap inquiry source can be expensive after duplicate scrubs and missing pharmacy evidence, while a higher-priced source can win through verified documents and shorter correction cycles. Compare sources only after their replacement windows mature; otherwise recent cohorts receive an artificial advantage. Use permissioned Looker Studio or spreadsheet reporting on aggregated identifiers rather than exposing claimant medical histories to broad dashboards. Require counsel to update intake criteria when scientific evidence, venue rulings, or Rule 702 decisions change the docket's viability. Stop the affected campaign while the contract's service and replacement consequences are assessed. Reforecast cash weekly, margins monthly, and capacity before every material spending increase. Keep annual scenarios on unrounded numbers and round only presentation cells; repeating monthly averages must reconcile to the exact annual totals. The scalable asset is a measured administrative production system with lawyer-controlled legal decisions, not a speculative warehouse of future settlements. Fund that system from earned service economics and committed liquidity, then increase volume only when both remain intact.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, ranked #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns legal intake and medical-record administration into a small-team service business, not a claim on settlements. Across its 13 mapped plays, this chapter prioritizes reserve-first capitalization, consent-evidenced call routing, and auditable HITECH triage. Keep at least half of $12,000–$50,000 startup capital liquid; release implementation spending only against contracted work and tested delivery. Canonical annual owner profits are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. The $2,500–$14,000 monthly operating envelope supports a controlled launch, not unlimited acquisition or mature delivery expense. Separate fixed administrative fees, source costs, retrieval outlays, and collection timing before hiring or increasing media commitments.
