sections.heading: 1. Ring-fence working capital before buying production capacity
paragraphs: Start with a cash waterfall rather than a shopping list. At $12,000, place $6,000 in a separate operating-reserve account and allocate the remaining $6,000 across formation, contract design, insurance deposits, systems, and a bounded acquisition test. At $50,000, retain $27,500 and deploy $22,500; the reserve shares are respectively 50% and 55%. These are capitalization examples, not expenses that recur every month. Reserve money covers retrieval advances, contractor invoices, disputed source charges, and slow firm payments. It does not fund speculative claim inventory or founder distributions. With no collections, $6,000 supports only 2.4 months at $2,500 monthly burn; $27,500 supports about 1.96 months at $14,000. Because first deals can take one to four months, a lean launch requires pre-sold administrative work, reduced discretionary spending, or additional capital before the fourth month. Use a thirteen-week cash forecast with separate dates for service completion, invoice issuance, contractual payment, and actual receipt. Release the next spending tranche only when the forecast survives the largest customer's payment arriving thirty days late without borrowing claimant money or delaying required security work. A signed engagement without a funded purchase order is a sales milestone, not spendable liquidity.

Form the operating entity before signing advertising, staffing, or retrieval obligations. Obtain an EIN directly through the IRS, record beneficial ownership and authorized signers in the entity file, and confirm current filing duties rather than assuming every domestic entity has identical reporting requirements. Maintain separate operating, tax, and reserve bank accounts; all three contain company money, never client trust balances. Use dual authorization for vendor bank changes and reconcile each account weekly. Insurance shopping should cover cyber incident response, technology or professional errors, and general liability, with explicit questions about health information, subcontractors, advertising injury, and contractual liability exclusions. A cheap policy excluding the actual service is dead capital. The law-firm MSO agreement must reserve legal judgment, case acceptance, representation, and settlement decisions to lawyers. Describe administrative deliverables, staffing assumptions, fair-market fixed or cost-plus pricing, invoicing evidence, replacement limits, and termination assistance. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model; the controlling jurisdiction's adopted rules determine the permitted structure. Arizona ABS participation requires the applicable authorization and ownership structure, not an Arizona mailing address. Obtain state-specific treatment of advertising and referral compensation before committing source spend. Keep that assessment attached to the contract version actually signed by both operating parties.

Reconcile the launch budget to the scorecard without pretending that pilot overhead represents mature annual costs. Conservative revenue of $160,000 less $118,400 total expense produces $41,600 owner profit at 26%. Base revenue of $705,000 less $437,100 produces $267,900 at 38.0%; Scaled revenue of $1,250,000 less $625,000 produces $625,000 at 50%. The corresponding average monthly total costs are $9,866.67, $36,425, and $52,083.33, with rounding confined to the monthly display. Therefore, $2,500–$14,000 is a controlled startup operating envelope, not an all-in annualized ceiling for every scenario. Mature variable acquisition, contractors, retrieval, and delivery must fit the larger scorecard expense totals. Conservative and Base use one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time staff plus four contractors. Contractor count does not imply full-time hours. Define each person's scheduled capacity and escalation duty before using those headcounts in staffing claims. Recognized revenue is the contracted MSO service fee, excluding gross settlements and trust funds. sections.heading: 2. Assemble twelve layers without twelve uncontrolled subscriptions
paragraphs: Treat the twelve-layer matrix as an architecture map, not a requirement to purchase twelve premium subscriptions. Its exact dollar figures are planning inputs: familiar published tier baselines where identified, and explicitly labeled procurement allowances where vendors negotiate pricing. They are not verified current offers. Confirm region, annual commitment, minimum volume, taxes, support, eligible services, and signed contract terms before ordering. One seat at a historical $6 monthly annual-commitment baseline costs $72 per year; three seats cost $216, not $18 total annually. Metered storage and communications require their own usage estimates. Start with a single identity directory, one structured work queue, one protected document repository, and one accounting ledger. The CRM should hold case tokens, service status, and accountable owners rather than duplicated medical records. Neither a vendor brand nor encryption alone establishes HIPAA suitability. Determine whether the MSO is acting as a business associate in each relationship, execute required agreements, and use only covered services with appropriate configuration. A law firm handling health records is not automatically a HIPAA covered entity. Regardless of that classification, implement contractual confidentiality, access restrictions, incident duties, and applicable state protections for the records actually processed.

Map permissions to work, not seniority. Intake contractors need contact verification and scheduling fields; retrieval staff need signed directions and provider destinations; clinical reviewers need the relevant record pages; finance needs service completion and invoice references. Require individual accounts, multifactor authentication, managed devices, and immediate offboarding. Store the identity-to-case-token mapping separately from advertising analytics. Do not place full Social Security numbers in routing payloads, spreadsheets, or model prompts. Where identity verification is justified, a contracted LexisNexis workflow can return a limited result under an appropriate permitted purpose and agreement; it does not replace the law firm's duplicate-retainer check. TrustedForm and Jornaya artifacts document aspects of a disclosure journey, not independent legal validity. Preserve the disclosure text, named recipient, timestamp, source, consumer action, and subsequent revocation in a linked evidence package. Keep medical documents out of ordinary marketing email, free consumer file links, and unapproved transcription services. CloudTrail event history alone does not record every object read; configure relevant data events and retention explicitly. Test a contractor account against another firm's records and require access denial before loading live files. Budget for log storage and incident investigation rather than discovering their absence after a misdirected attachment.

Automate chronology drafting only after retrieval and evidence handling work manually. OCR output should preserve page references, document dates, provider names, medication units, and uncertainty about illegible text. An ICD-10 code supports classification; it does not establish product exposure, diagnosis accuracy, or legal causation. A model-generated timeline must cite the source page and separate patient reporting from clinician findings. Require human review of identity matches, exposure dates, contradictory records, and every conclusion sent to the law firm. Use an approved service configuration with the necessary contractual protections or a suitably secured local deployment; a consumer chat subscription is not the production architecture. To compare costs, assume 100 files require twenty minutes each manually: 33.33 reviewer hours. If extraction reduces review to twelve minutes, the workload becomes twenty hours, saving 13.33 hours. At $45 per hour, gross labor savings approach $600 before inference, OCR, exception handling, and quality sampling. Spend less than that verified saving on automation at this volume. Disable extraction when page linkage fails or error rates rise, returning the affected cohort to manual chronology preparation. Maintain a small labeled evaluation set that includes duplicate names, missing pages, contradictory dates, and pharmacy substitutions rather than testing only clean demonstration records.

sections.heading: 3. Price the complete evidence waterfall, not cheap inquiries
paragraphs: Track raw inquiry -> signed law-firm retainer -> usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof -> deficiency-free accepted case -> collected MSO/vendor fee as distinct operational events. Add duplicate and identity rejection between inquiry and retainer, but never erase rejected records from source-quality denominators. In a bounded example, 100 inquiries at $20 cost $2,000. A twenty-percent duplicate or identity rejection leaves eighty; a fifty-percent signing rate produces forty retainers. Spend $35 per retrieval attempt, or $1,400, across those forty. If twenty-five percent lack qualifying proof, thirty remain. A twenty-percent deficiency failure leaves twenty-four deficiency-free cases. Add $900 of documented administrative labor, bringing cohort delivery and acquisition cost to $4,300. A separately negotiated $6,000 fixed administrative pilot then yields $1,700 contribution before shared overhead, provided the work was performed and the invoice collects. The twenty-four cases measure service efficiency; they do not establish a lawful per-case referral price. Cost per deficiency-free case is $179.17, while fixed pilot contribution is 28.33% of its fee. Neither figure is an annual scorecard margin. Recognize service revenue under the contract's performance obligations rather than when a claimant signs a retainer or when a future settlement becomes imaginable. Keep invoice collection status visible beside operational acceptance.

Stress the same cohort before increasing media spend. If duplicates rise to thirty-five percent, sixty-five inquiries remain and thirty-two sign in this integer planning case. At $35 each, retrieval costs $1,120. If only sixteen produce qualifying records and twelve survive deficiencies, the unchanged $2,000 media spend plus $900 labor produces $4,020 cost, or $335 per deficiency-free case. Four additional retrieval attempts during a thirty-day replacement window add $140, raising total cost to $4,160 and unit cost to $346.67. A $6,000 fixed fee still produces $1,840 contribution before overhead if the contracted administrative scope was delivered; that arithmetic does not justify promising case counts. Lower output may cause nonrenewal, service disputes, or additional contractual work. If only $4,800 has collected, immediate cash surplus is $640 and $1,200 remains receivable; delayed payment alone does not automatically reduce recognized revenue. Specify whether replacement means repeating an administrative task, correcting a document deficiency, or crediting a defective bill. Avoid unlimited obligations to supply new claimants. For patient access under 45 CFR 164.524, track receipt, identity validation, the thirty-day response deadline, and any permitted written extension. Distinguish patient-access requests, third-party directions, and 45 CFR 164.508 authorizations; fee limits and third-party rights are not interchangeable after Ciox.

The mapped play inbound_rtb_pay_per_call_ping_post_exchange uses Ringba or Retreaver buyer integrations and sub-second ping-post trees to compare permitted buyer offers. Send a minimal payload such as campaign token, general geography, and service category, not a diagnosis, full identity, or medical document. In a separately authorized nonlegal vertical, twenty genuinely accepted calls at a $90 buyer payout generate $1,800 billings; $1,100 traffic acquisition and $100 routing cost leave $600 contribution before overhead. Apply principal-agent accounting before calling the $1,800 recognized revenue. A negotiated ninety-to-120-second trigger is only one payment condition alongside caller intent, buyer acceptance, and contract terms. Do not transplant that referral-spread model into mass-tort legal intake where compensation is prohibited; use approved fixed or cost-plus administrative pricing instead. Keep ACA/Medicare, auto/home insurance, legal intake, and emergency home services in separate programs, each with its own recipient disclosures and transfer restrictions. Require recipient-specific consent where applicable and use one-recipient disclosure as an operating standard, without describing the vacated FCC one-to-one rule as current federal law. TrustedForm or Jornaya supports evidence, not validity by itself. Stop defective sources and transfers, preserve evidence securely, refund invalid billings, and resume only after corrected disclosures, permitted compensation, and verified buyer acceptance.

sections.heading: 4. Prove readiness with failure tests and a funded launch sequence
paragraphs: Run a pre-flight exercise using synthetic claimants before accepting production records. Walk one clean inquiry through disclosure capture, firm-directed intake, retainer status, authorized retrieval, chronology preparation, deficiency resolution, and administrative invoicing. Then repeat with a duplicate identity, revoked contact permission, mismatched pharmacy record, missing signature, and wrong recipient. Each defect needs a named owner, a queue status, and a documented next action. A signed retainer belongs to the firm's representation workflow; the MSO must not sign for the lawyer, decide legal eligibility, or imply that administrative screening establishes representation. Validate call recording requirements for the relevant states separately from TCPA contact permission. Confirm that provider requests identify the correct patient, scope, destination, and authority without collecting unrelated history by default. Ask the customer to accept or reject a sample chronology against written criteria before authorizing paid volume. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 and an MDL court's causation decisions can change the commercial value of a campaign overnight; they do not transform administrative staff into expert witnesses. Assign a lawyer at the customer firm to monitor litigation developments and notify operations when qualifying criteria or campaign continuation changes. Record those instructions as versioned operating requirements.

Test cash collection and failure recovery as seriously as intake conversion. Generate a sample invoice with the contract identifier, service period, agreed deliverables, approved expenses, payment instructions, and supporting completion references. Confirm the law firm's payable contact and purchase-order requirements before work starts. A thirty-day replacement window combined with thirty-day payment terms can lock up cash longer than expected when acceptance occurs after service delivery; model the actual contractual sequence rather than adding convenient calendar labels. Establish a weekly reconciliation joining source charges, provider invoices, contractor time, service milestones, customer credits, and bank receipts by cohort. Rehearse disabling a compromised account, isolating a misdirected document, restoring an encrypted backup, and exporting the current work queue during vendor downtime. Write recovery objectives that the small team can actually meet, such as restoring the active queue within one business day and recovering document versions through the prior day's snapshot. These are initial service design targets, not claims of tested performance. Time the exercise and record the result. If restoration fails, postpone sensitive production work while continuing contract negotiation and synthetic testing. Manual fallback means controlled authorized processing, not emailing unprotected records to a contractor's personal account.

Launch one funded customer, one approved campaign, and one measurable service scope. During the first two weeks, review every chronology and every source exception; reduce sampling only after measured error rates justify it. Monitor duplicate share, signed-retainer conversion, retrieval age, qualifying-proof yield, deficiency-free acceptance, replacement cost, invoice age, and cash collected. Cap daily commitments at the smaller of available delivery capacity and forecast-funded purchasing authority. If ten files require twelve reviewer minutes each, budget two hours of review plus intake, retrieval follow-up, and exception work; do not describe two hours as total case labor. Review capacity with the actual contractor schedule before increasing traffic. Add the second employee only when contracted recurring contribution covers salary, payroll burden, equipment, and the desired reserve replenishment. Keep nonlegal exchange experiments separately costed so their attractive call spreads cannot hide losses in medical-record delivery. Suspend a legal campaign when firm instructions change, identity defects cluster, retrieval quality collapses, or invoices exceed the agreed credit limit. Reopen only after the specific defect is corrected and verified. Capital discipline is the repeated decision to buy the next reliable unit of service capacity instead of an impressive dashboard, premature headcount, or a larger uncollectible book of invoices.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46 ranks #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 13 mapped plays. Its attractive economics depend on selling documented administrative work, not monetizing settlement percentages or counting signed retainers as collected revenue. The canonical annual owner profits are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. This chapter isolates the failures that consume those profits: synthetic inquiries, duplicate representation, nonqualifying medical evidence, retrieval overruns, replacement liabilities, advertising restrictions, and concentrated MDL exposure. Follow one auditable waterfall from raw inquiry to collected MSO fee. Use cohort-based defect reserves, buyer-specific contact authorization, fixed-fee scope controls, and immediate spend suspension when evidence quality or lawful delivery fails.

sections.heading: 1. Break the Retainer Illusion Before It Becomes a Replacement Liability
paragraphs: The question's 80% framing is a stress-test prompt, not an established industry failure statistic. The first fatal trap is treating a signed retainer as finished inventory. A claimant can sign twice, misremember a product, lack qualifying exposure, or produce records inconsistent with the intake script. Instrument the complete waterfall: raw inquiry -> signed law-firm retainer -> usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof -> deficiency-free accepted case -> collected MSO/vendor fee. Add duplicate and identity dispositions before representation, but keep the original inquiry denominator visible. A weekly dashboard should show both stage conversion and elapsed days by campaign, vendor, receiving firm, and injury theory. Never combine fresh inquiries with mature accepted cases to manufacture a favorable conversion rate. Record acceptance as the firm's documented operational disposition, not an MSO opinion about legal merit. Trap two is buying exclusive leads without defining exclusivity: a vendor may exclude other buyers while the claimant already has counsel. Require provenance, a claimant-confirmed representation question, and a receiving-firm conflict procedure. Treat LexisNexis identity matches and duplicate signals as investigation inputs, not conclusive fraud findings. A shared telephone number can reflect a household, while a unique number can still conceal a fabricated identity.

Build a reproducible illustrative cohort before raising budgets. Ten thousand clicks at $0.08 cost $800 and produce 400 raw inquiries at a 4% form conversion rate. Suppose 80 inquiries fail duplicate or identity screening, leaving 320; 128 sign firm retainers, 80 yield usable evidence, and 64 become deficiency-free accepted cases. The raw-to-accepted yield is 16%, not the 40% clean-inquiry-to-retainer conversion shown in a vendor pitch. At an illustrative $35 retrieval outlay for each of the 128 requests, records cost $4,480. Advertising plus retrieval already totals $5,280, or $82.50 per accepted case, before intake labor, software, and overhead. If the firm pays a separately negotiated $12,000 fixed monthly administrative invoice for the documented scope, the cohort's allocation is $187.50 per accepted case; that allocation is a management metric, not the contract price for procuring a client. Suppose $2,000 is disputed: cash collected is $10,000 while recognized revenue depends on performance, enforceable terms, and any required credit adjustment. Never count the claimant's potential award or the firm's contingent fee in this MSO waterfall. Preserve separate service revenue, receivables, credits, and cash fields.

Trap three is an unlimited replacement promise disguised as vendor confidence. Define an administrative defect precisely: missing required authorization, duplicated delivery within the contracted scope, or an omitted document the operator agreed to retrieve. Do not promise replacement merely because litigation strategy changes or a medically genuine claimant fails counsel's legal criteria. A 30-day documentary defect window and a separate deadline for submitting supporting evidence create a measurable exposure period; the actual terms must match the firm's purchasing rules and applicable professional obligations. Price documented rework rather than hiding it in an indefinite free-replacement pool. For internal planning, 100 delivered service files with an 8% historical rework rate and $60 incremental remediation cost require $480 of expected rework capacity. That operational estimate does not automatically determine the accounting treatment of refunds or credits. Suspend a source when confirmed duplicates exceed 10% of its last 50 screened inquiries, or when material provenance failures recur twice in one week. These are starting control limits, not industry benchmarks. Review false positives with the firm before restarting spend, and maintain a dated exception log so a vendor cannot erase a bad cohort by issuing replacement IDs.

callout.title: Four Controls Experienced Intake Operators Install First
callout.body: Preserve evidence at the original event and measure mature cohorts; reconstructed explanations rarely resolve contested invoices.
items: Use keyed identity tokens for cross-cohort duplicate detection; restrict raw identifiers to the authorized verification workspace and retain a false-positive review path.

sections.heading: 2. Replace Fragile Feed Economics Without Buying a Referral or a Platform Ban
paragraphs: The mapped play social_to_search_ping_post_arbitrage replaces fragile $1.50 RSOC/AFD search-feed clicks with direct $45–$180 Ping-Post lead-auction economics after buying $0.05–$0.12 curiosity clicks on Meta, TikTok, NewsBreak, and native ad networks. Those figures describe the play's pricing assumptions, not verified current platform offers or permission to auction legal clients. Its four-question bridge should collect only location, a broad product or exposure category, existing representation status, and permission for contact by the specifically identified receiving firm. Move detailed diagnoses, treatment dates, and documents into the authorized private intake environment. At 10,000 clicks, media costs range from $500 to $1,200. If 400 forms produce 40 legally permissible, contractually accepted advertising deliveries, the quoted price range implies $1,800–$7,200 in gross receipts before rejection, labor, retrieval, and refunds. Do not add those receipts to the preceding fixed-fee example; they are alternative commercial structures. The legal-services version requires jurisdiction-specific analysis of referral payments, solicitation, advertising, and fee sharing. If a transaction is prohibited client procurement, calling it marketing does not cure it. Use a fair-market fixed-scope advertising or MSO arrangement instead when that structure is permissible.

Trap four is thinking a consent certificate authorizes every buyer. TrustedForm and Jornaya can help preserve session evidence, but a certificate is neither proof that every statement was truthful nor blanket permission for unrelated firms to call. Capture the exact displayed language, identified recipient, form version, timestamp, and affirmative action; preserve the provider's certificate reference and available verification artifacts, with a cryptographic digest of your own immutable evidence bundle. A missing bundle means no delivery. The FCC's 2023 federal one-to-one lead-generation consent restriction was vacated in 2025; do not represent it as an operative nationwide mandate. Buyer-specific authorization remains this operation's contractual design, while actual obligations depend on 47 U.S.C. § 227, operative 47 CFR § 64.1200 provisions, calling technology, message content, and state law. Honor revocation and applicable do-not-call restrictions across vendors. Diversify commercial relationships across five or more direct buyers without broadcasting one claimant's sensitive facts to all five. Route only after identifying the intended recipient and obtaining the necessary permission. A ping should disclose the minimum permitted routing attributes, not a medical narrative, full identity record, or unredacted authorization document.

Trap five is using blackhat acquisition shortcuts to repair weak economics: fabricated testimonials, fake government notices, invented settlement deadlines, misleading compensation calculators, cloaked landing pages, and replacement accounts after suspension. These tactics can produce account termination, uncollectible invoices, and claims that exceed an entire year's contribution. Enforce 100% factual ad hooks, with a source record for each numerical or medical assertion. Do not imply that a visitor has a disease or that exposure establishes eligibility. Maintain matching creative, destination content, and receiving-firm identity; inspect current Meta and TikTok sensitive-information restrictions before publishing. Never place diagnosis, medication, claim narrative, or retainer status in pixel parameters, URLs, or audience uploads. Treat any verified sensitive-data transmission to an advertising destination as a reason to disable that integration immediately and investigate scope. Pause a creative after its first substantiated deception complaint rather than waiting for a platform strike. Monitor cost per collected service dollar, not cheap clicks: $800 media plus $1,600 intake labor against $1,800 collected receipts is already a $600 loss before records. Restart only with corrected content, authorized routing, and a documented small-budget test on the existing legitimate account.

sections.heading: 3. Stop Retrieval Costs and Clinical Parsing Errors from Compounding
paragraphs: Trap six is assuming that every record request is a cheap, immediate HITECH download. Under 45 CFR § 164.524, an individual's access right generally reaches protected health information in the designated record set, subject to specified exceptions. Covered entities generally must act within 30 days and may take one additional 30-day extension with the required timely written explanation and completion date. That is not a universal vendor delivery promise. Distinguish an individual access request, a qualifying patient-directed electronic transmission, and a third-party authorization request under 45 CFR § 164.508. Following Ciox, do not assume the individual-access fee limitation applies to every third-party delivery. Map request authority, recipient, requested format, identity verification, and applicable fee rules before submission. Use a signed authorization when that is the appropriate route, rather than impersonating the patient in a portal. Request the relevant dates, medication history, pathology, and exposure-supporting documents without buying an entire lifetime chart by default. Confirm whether responsive electronic information is maintained and whether the requested form is readily producible. Track provider acknowledgment, quotation, due date, extension, receipt, and missing components separately; an automated reminder does not establish that the request was valid.

Trap seven is paying repeatedly for evidence that cannot satisfy the firm's written case criteria. Establish an evidence map before ordering: alleged exposure, product identity, diagnosis, timing, and required source document. A pharmacy fill does not independently prove ingestion, a billing code does not establish causation, and a problem-list entry may be copied forward. An LLM ICD-10 and exposure-timeline parser should extract source-linked observations, preserve negation, distinguish historical conditions from active findings, and flag contradictory dates. It must not upgrade uncertain language into a confirmed diagnosis or make legal eligibility decisions. Require page-level citations and human verification of every material eligibility fact before firm delivery. Measure parser disagreement against reviewed samples, not model confidence scores. With 128 requests at $35, the $4,480 retrieval budget becomes $6,400 if average cost rises to $50, consuming another $1,920 before acceptance changes. If accepted files fall from 64 to 48, media plus the higher retrieval spend becomes $7,200, or $150 per accepted file. Set a quote exception at $50 for this illustrative cohort and pause the source when usable-proof yield falls below 50% of mature completed retrievals. Reassess the threshold against the actual fixed-fee scope and documented case-selection criteria.

Trap eight is treating an MSO's software stack as exempt from health information controls because the customer is a law firm. HIPAA status depends on functions and relationships; a law firm or vendor is not automatically a covered entity or business associate merely because it holds medical records. Where business-associate status applies, execute the required agreement and bind applicable subcontractors before handling protected information. Independently map professional confidentiality, contracts, and applicable state privacy requirements. Use encrypted storage, individual identities, role-based permissions, audit events, and documented retention schedules. Do not send charts into consumer chat accounts or a model endpoint whose retention and contract terms have not been approved for the actual data relationship. Keep parser output within the same controlled workspace as source documents. Require a second reviewer for contradictory exposure dates or material diagnosis conflicts. One cross-claimant document merge requires immediate delivery suspension for the affected pipeline, access containment, and incident assessment; a mass resend compounds the event. Delete or retain records according to the governing schedule and applicable preservation obligations, not a generic cleanup timer. Test retrieval and chronology exports with controlled sample records before onboarding a new contractor.

sections.heading: 4. Ring-Fence Causation Shocks, Fee-Splitting Exposure, and Cash Exhaustion
paragraphs: Trap nine is transferring the firm's litigation risk onto an administrative balance sheet. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 requires the proponent to establish admissibility requirements more likely than not, including reliable application of reliable principles and methods. A general-causation exclusion can damage an entire MDL acquisition thesis even when every claimant is real and every chart is authentic. Track campaign exposure by product, injury theory, docket, firm, and expected service collection date. Use PACER docket events and the responsible firm's written updates to monitor expert deadlines, dispositive rulings, and changes in intake criteria. Do not let an ad buyer interpret an expert ruling into a new legal theory. An illustrative concentration limit is 35% of forward 90-day contracted service revenue tied to one causation thesis, with any excess explicitly funded by available cash reserves. A material adverse ruling stops new discretionary acquisition for that cohort until the firm issues updated instructions. Continue necessary preservation and contracted client service rather than abandoning files. Avoid provisions making otherwise completed administrative work refundable solely because settlements disappear; that term can turn a seemingly fixed-fee contract into unbounded litigation exposure.

Trap ten is believing that an MSO label neutralizes professional-conduct rules. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model, and controlling state rules and exceptions must be checked for each arrangement. Set fair-market fixed or cost-plus prices for genuine marketing, intake administration, records, and technology services; document deliverables and cost allocations. A percentage of legal fees, settlement-linked bonus, or control over attorney judgment cannot be rescued by changing the invoice description. Separate the firm's client selection, legal advice, strategy, and representation decisions from MSO execution. Arizona's licensed ABS regime is a specific regulated structure, not a portable exemption for nationwide nonlawyer fee sharing. Verify the entity's license and the actual jurisdictional scope before relying on it. State runner restrictions also matter; California Business and Professions Code §§ 6151–6153 provides a concrete example of prohibited client solicitation arrangements. Never train intake staff to promise case value, coach exposure answers, or pressure claimants to abandon existing counsel. Trap eleven is letting the MSO touch client trust funds or gross settlement awards. Keep those entirely outside operator revenue, treasury access, and performance dashboards.

Trap twelve is scaling from booked revenue while cash and defect liabilities diverge. The canonical Formula v2.0 cases remain $160,000 revenue at 26% margin for $41,600 owner profit; $705,000 at 38.0% for $267,900; and $1,250,000 at 50% for $625,000. Implied total annual expenses are $118,400, $437,100, and $625,000 respectively. Teams remain 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C. The $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex range does not replace those full expense totals; reconcile its defined scope with variable acquisition, retrieval, and contractor costs. On the Base case, an illustrative 5% service credit reduces revenue by $35,250, and $20,000 additional rework reduces profit to $212,650 if other costs remain unchanged. That is a 30.5% margin on adjusted revenue of $669,750, not a replacement canonical scenario. Thirty extra collection days on evenly earned Base revenue can tie up about $57,945 without initially changing profit. Maintain a rolling 13-week cash forecast and stop discretionary acquisition when unrestricted cash cannot cover eight weeks of committed outlays plus estimated credits. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to pass-through arrangements; gross cash handled is not automatically recognized operator revenue.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, ranked #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns fragmented plaintiff-intake operations into contracted administrative capacity. Across 13 mapped plays, this chapter concentrates on demand mining, consent-first screening, HITECH evidence retrieval, and fixed-fee law-firm MSO engagements. Find firms facing documented intake backlogs, sell a bounded operational pilot, and measure every transition from inquiry to collected service fees without pricing access to claimants or sharing legal recoveries. Canonical annual owner profits are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. The first 3-to-10 wins should be signed, paid administrative mandates within 1–4 months, supported by buyer qualification, auditable consent, usable records, and explicit replacement limits rather than speculative settlement values.

sections.heading: 1. Mine operating pressure rather than claimant identities
paragraphs: Start with law firms whose public activity implies a specific administrative bottleneck, not a presumed willingness to buy claimants. Review the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation's published MDL statistics, then inspect the relevant federal court's case-management orders through PACER. Record census deadlines, plaintiff fact-sheet requirements, deficiency procedures, and newly appointed leadership counsel. These events create demand for document indexing, authorized retrieval, intake scheduling, and exception management; they do not establish that any individual qualifies for relief. Cross-check firm websites, attorney directories, LinkedIn hiring notices, Google Ads Transparency Center, and Meta Ad Library for active campaigns and intake hiring. A firm advertising across three jurisdictions while recruiting records coordinators deserves investigation before a dormant firm with a prestigious verdict page. Build a company-level research ledger containing source URL, observation date, jurisdiction, responsible business contact, operational hypothesis, and next verification question. Keep claimant names and medical facts out of this prospecting ledger. Public filing access does not justify republishing sensitive allegations or using a health condition to target an individual. Capture only the minimum business signal needed to explain why a defined service could remove a measurable queue.

Allocate the first research sprint to forty firms across two active dockets and one geographic operating cluster. Score each account on five dimensions worth twenty points apiece: documented deadline pressure, observable intake volume, records backlog, accessible operating sponsor, and ability to purchase a fixed administrative scope. Award twenty points only for direct evidence, ten for a corroborated inference, and zero when evidence is absent. Pursue accounts scoring at least seventy after a discovery conversation confirms budget and a responsible lawyer. A high public signal score never substitutes for buyer confirmation. Ask how many authorized requests remain open, the oldest unresolved request age, the current retrieval cost, and who decides whether evidence satisfies the firm's criteria. Request aggregate counts before requesting any patient information. Disqualify demands for purchased signatures, payment tied to recovery, undisclosed referral compensation, or unrestricted access to another firm's claimant database. An incumbent vendor is not a dead end: propose overflow capacity for one provider network or one document category with explicit ownership boundaries. Your strongest opening is a documented operational discrepancy, such as growing fact-sheet obligations without corresponding records staffing, followed by a narrow offer to measure and clear that discrepancy.

Convert each signal into an evidence-backed offer sheet before sending outreach. For a fact-sheet deadline, offer a ten-business-day document inventory and exception queue. For a provider backlog, offer an authorized request-status desk with daily aging reports. For an advertising expansion, offer consent-evidence reconciliation and duplicate detection before new contacts enter the dialing system. For a Rule 702 development, offer administrative reclassification under criteria supplied by counsel, never an independent prediction of causation or settlement value. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 and Daubert-related exclusions can collapse acquisition economics even when intake conversion remains strong. Require the firm to identify which campaigns should pause when a material order changes its strategy. Separate recurring service demand from speculative litigation demand by asking whether the task remains useful if new advertising stops. Indexing existing records usually does; purchasing another batch of unverified inquiries may not. Price the diagnostic as a fixed scope that produces a queue map, sample audit, and remediation estimate. Do not provide free patient-level processing merely to win access. The initial asset is a repeatable operating relationship with a solvent buyer, not an inventory of prospective plaintiffs.

callout.title: Find the buyer behind the visible litigation signal
callout.body: Public activity earns a discovery question; verified operating friction earns a proposal. Preserve that distinction throughout sourcing.
items: Save the exact case-management order and deadline paragraph, then ask the operations sponsor which internal queue owns the resulting work.
Ask for an aggregate provider-aging histogram before negotiating retrieval pricing; a few unresponsive custodians can dominate labor cost.

sections.heading: 2. Build a consent-first screening offer without selling permission
paragraphs: The mapped play tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage belongs to TRACK_2, but its defensible implementation is a consent-first screening service, not a device for contacting people who appear unlikely to sue. Use lawfully accessed docket-derived risk signals only as a secondary review input alongside authoritative do-not-call suppression, revocation records, number reassignment checks where applicable, and the required consent evidence for the proposed technology and message. Never build deceptive honeypots or contact a person because they were absent from a litigation list. A plaintiff-name match neither authorizes contact nor proves abuse; common names, stale telephone numbers, and unrelated proceedings create obvious false positives. Restrict enrichment to a documented purpose, approved access method, and minimal retention period. When matching confidence is weak, disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks. Record the reason for every blocked or released contact. TrustedForm can preserve evidence about a submitted form, but a certificate alone does not establish that the disclosure covered the actual seller, communication method, or later campaign. LexisNexis identity services likewise require appropriate access and permitted use; they do not provide universal visibility into competing law-firm retainers.

Package screening around processing capacity and documented work. An illustrative monthly scope covers ten thousand submitted contact records for a $2,400 fixed administrative fee. At an assumed $0.06 per record for permitted verification inputs, data costs equal $600; twenty analyst hours at $30 cost another $600; allocated tooling and secure hosting add $300. The resulting $900 contribution is 37.5% before other business overhead, not a replacement for the volume's canonical owner-profit scenarios. Supplier prices must be quoted before contracting. If ambiguous matches double analyst time, contribution falls to $300, or 12.5%; cap the exception queue and sell additional authorized capacity through a written scope change. The fallback is suppression and evidence verification without docket enrichment, not relaxed contact standards. Keep records of inputs, rule versions, dispositions, and manual corrections so the buyer can reproduce a decision. Do not publish accusatory labels about individuals or use the service to conceal unlawful outreach. A screening product is valuable because it documents lawful operating decisions and catches broken evidence chains, not because it promises immunity from a complaint or identifies people whose rights matter less.

Separate business-development outreach to firm personnel from claimant communications commissioned by the firm. For business email, use accurate sender details, truthful subjects, the required postal address, and a functioning opt-out under 15 U.S.C. § 7704; maintain suppression across campaigns. A publicly listed mobile number is not permission for automated marketing calls or texts. Apply 47 U.S.C. § 227, 47 CFR § 64.1200, and relevant state requirements to the actual channel and technology. Treat seller-specific, one-to-one consent as an operating standard rather than claiming that the FCC's vacated 2023 one-to-one amendment currently supplies a universal federal requirement. Preserve the precise disclosure, named recipient, timestamp, source page, and subsequent revocation history. Counsel should approve claimant-facing scripts and jurisdictional advertising disclosures before use. Nonlawyer personnel may collect facts and arrange attorney contact but must not assess legal rights, promise recovery, or pressure signatures. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model framework; binding state rules control the engagement. A licensed Arizona alternative business structure changes only what its actual authorization permits. It does not automatically extend fee-sharing authority across states or to an unaffiliated marketing vendor that invokes the structure in a proposal.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile the entire evidence waterfall before quoting capacity
paragraphs: Use one cohort ledger to track raw inquiry to signed law-firm retainer to usable HITECH EMR or pharmacy proof to deficiency-free accepted case to collected MSO/vendor fee. Keep the last stage at the service-contract level: fees compensate administrative work, not the presence of a retained claimant or a recovery. An illustrative cohort starts with 200 inquiries, loses forty duplicates or invalid submissions, and produces 84 retainers from 160 unique inquiries, a 52.5% signing rate. Request authorized records for all 84; forty-two produce usable proof, a 50% evidence yield. Counsel accepts thirty-four after eight files remain deficient, an 81.0% acceptance rate from usable proof and 17% from raw inquiries. The fixed administrative pilot earns $8,000 for the contracted service period; $6,000 has been collected and $2,000 remains receivable. Collection is therefore 75% of invoiced fees, not thirty-four case sales. Log retainer execution separately from legal acceptance, and never treat either as an administrative worker's legal judgment. Maintain dated exclusion reasons so the firm can distinguish duplicate records, deficient authority, missing exposure evidence, clinical mismatch, and outstanding provider responses rather than compressing every loss into a misleading lead-quality percentage.

Under 45 CFR § 164.524, distinguish an individual's access request from a third-party disclosure authorization under § 164.508. The usual access response deadline is thirty days, with one additional thirty-day extension when the required written explanation and completion date are supplied. Shorter applicable state deadlines and record-specific rules require separate tracking. Electronic delivery depends on the records held and the requested form being readily producible. Do not describe HITECH as an automatic extraction API or assume every law-firm request receives the individual-access fee limit. Ciox-related limits distinguish third-party directions from personal access, including the scope of electronic health-record directions; select the correct pathway and budget the actual permitted charge. Pharmacy histories may identify dispensing dates without establishing ingestion, dose adherence, or causation. Use an LLM chronology parser only within approved data-handling arrangements, with source-page citations and human verification of dates, product names, and negation. ICD-10 codes help organize records but do not independently prove exposure or case eligibility. Prohibit unsupported inference from a missing page. Route clinical ambiguity to qualified reviewers and eligibility decisions to counsel, while keeping the administrative queue moving on undisputed indexing tasks.

Budget the illustrative $8,000 pilot with $2,400 intake labor, $2,100 retrieval outlays at $25 for each of 84 requests, $800 quality review, and $300 screening tools. Total direct cost is $5,600, leaving $2,400 before other overhead; this 30% pilot contribution is distinct from annual net margin. Stress duplicates to 35% of inquiries: 130 unique inquiries yield approximately 68 retainers at the same signing rate. If usable proof falls to 35%, approximately 24 files have proof and nineteen reach acceptance. At $45 per request, retrieval costs become $3,060; add $800 rework to unchanged intake, review, and tooling costs for $7,360 total direct cost and only $640 contribution. A fourteen-calendar-day correction window should cover documented vendor processing errors, not free replacement of claimants whose evidence fails legal criteria. Canonical annual revenue bridges are twenty $8,000 service-months for $160,000, forty-seven $15,000 service-months for $705,000, and fifty $25,000 service-months for $1,250,000. These are illustrative capacity packages, not case prices. Formula v2.0 total costs remain $118,400, $437,100, and $625,000, yielding owner profits of $41,600, $267,900, and $625,000. Recognize agency pass-throughs net when required by ASC 606; exclude settlements, trust funds, and client advertising spend controlled and purchased directly by the firm.

sections.heading: 4. Run a four-month cadence that closes paid administrative mandates
paragraphs: Run an account-based cadence against verified business contacts rather than a bulk claimant list. On day one, send a short email citing one public operating trigger and offering one bounded diagnostic. On day four, place a lawful manual call to the published business line and ask who owns the records queue. On day eight, share a synthetic example of an aging report or chronology exception register through the channel the contact accepts. On day fifteen, send a concise close-the-loop message with an opt-out and stop further campaign outreach when requested. Use LinkedIn for relevant professional engagement, not automated message flooding. Build inbound demand with a provider-delay calculator, a fact-sheet readiness checklist, and a webinar co-presented with a properly engaged lawyer who owns legal interpretations. Forms should request company and workflow information, not public uploads of medical records. Send sensitive documents only through the approved secure intake channel after authority is established. Attribute inbound inquiries to the originating content and the actual buyer role. A hundred downloads from claimants are not equivalent to three qualified conversations with operations directors who control budget and can authorize a paid diagnostic.

Use explicit planning benchmarks rather than presenting invented market averages. An initial four-month target is 120 researched firms, ninety with verified business contacts, twenty-seven substantive replies, eighteen discovery meetings, nine qualified scopes, six signed pilots, and five funded starts. Those assumptions imply a 30% reply rate from contacted accounts, 66.7% meeting conversion from replies, 50% scope conversion from meetings, 66.7% signing from scopes, and 83.3% funding from signed pilots. Five funded starts equal 4.2% of researched accounts. If the first thirty contacted accounts produce fewer than three substantive replies, inspect trigger quality, deliverability, and buyer selection before increasing volume. If meetings occur but scopes stall, require a budget owner and quantified backlog before drafting another proposal. Three wins can be reached with fewer productive accounts; ten requires stronger conversion, more qualified accounts, or a longer cycle, not weaker verification. Define a win as an executed administrative mandate with its required initial payment received. A verbal commitment, unsigned statement of work, or unfunded retainer is pipeline. Track days between each stage and record the buyer's stated loss reason to separate pricing problems from missing authority, procurement delay, and insufficient demand.

Close objections by changing scope or evidence, never by changing the compensation into a disguised legal contingency. When a firm requests payment only for signed cases, offer a fixed capacity block with transparent activity reporting and capped correction credits for administrative errors. When it already uses a vendor, isolate one overflow queue and reconcile ownership daily. When price is challenged, compare the buyer's documented labor and retrieval costs against a smaller pilot rather than asserting universal savings. When a buyer asks for unrestricted database access, demonstrate synthetic output and request a minimized, authorized sample through the secure channel. The statement of work should define deliverables, provider-delay exceptions, counsel-owned eligibility criteria, retrieval authorization, security responsibilities, invoice timing, termination, and data return. Schedule weekly operating reviews covering open requests, duplicate rates, evidence yield, accepted files, invoiced service dollars, and collected cash. In month one, validate demand and access controls; in month two, deliver paid pilots; in months three and four, convert successful pilots to recurring capacity. Keep startup deployment within the $12,000–$50,000 capital range and planned monthly operating spend within $2,500–$14,000 during launch. Those launch ranges do not replace the larger annual total-cost budgets required by the canonical operating scenarios.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, Rank #13 of 49, scores 93/100 across a shelf mapping of 13 plays. Execution depends on separating claimant evidence, attorney decisions, administrative service delivery, and collected cash. This chapter turns that separation into a production waterfall, six-module SQLite reference, and worked 90-day operating cohort. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled; none counts settlement awards or client trust funds as operator revenue. The Base illustration delivers $58,750 monthly contracted MSO revenue against $36,425 operating costs, then exposes the working-capital effect of split collections. Duplicate scrubs, record failures, replacement labor, and privacy-claim evidence receive explicit owners, stop conditions, and ledger treatment.

sections.heading: 1. Bind every intake transition to evidence, authority, and a named owner
paragraphs: Start with two separate agreements: the claimant's engagement with the law firm and the firm's administrative services agreement with the MSO. Counsel controls conflicts, representation, claim selection, litigation strategy, and termination; the MSO supplies documented marketing, intake coordination, retrieval, and chronology production. Price those services at supported fair-market fixed or cost-plus rates, never a percentage of recoveries or an accepted-case bounty disguised as administration. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model rather than a nationwide statute: confirm each relevant jurisdiction's adopted professional-conduct rules and advertising restrictions. An Arizona alternative business structure requires the applicable license and operating conditions; another state's matters do not automatically inherit that permission. Build the contractual service schedule before buying traffic, including capacity, deliverables, provider charges, rejection reasons, and a 30-day administrative correction window. Replacement work repairs deficient services; it does not promise a different plaintiff or a successful claim. Keep settlement proceeds, trust balances, and loan principal outside the MSO ledger entirely. Assign one full-time operator to scheduling and reconciliation, three contractors to intake, record handling, and evidence quality, and a separately retained law-firm reviewer to legal decisions. This allocation matches the Base team without treating outside counsel as MSO-controlled labor.

Instrument the complete waterfall before optimizing advertisements: raw inquiry, signed law-firm retainer, usable HITECH EMR or pharmacy proof, deficiency-free accepted case, and collected MSO fee. The worked monthly cohort starts with 1,000 inquiries, removes 200 duplicate or invalid submissions, signs 320 of 800 remaining contacts, obtains usable proof for 224, and finishes 200 counsel-accepted files after 24 further deficiencies. Those are operational counts, not invoice triggers. TrustedForm can preserve a submission's consent artifact; it cannot establish identity, erase contradictory contact instructions, or prove that another firm lacks a retainer. Use an authorized LexisNexis identity workflow where appropriate, claimant confirmation, and the firm's own conflict records rather than claiming a universal retainer database exists. Generate a firm-scoped keyed identity token only after verification, and manually examine probable matches before linking records. Keep raw SSNs outside the administrative ledger. Capture the specific firm's contact permission, disclosure version, source URL, timestamp, and revocation history. Firm-specific permission is the operating standard here, not an assertion that a vacated FCC one-to-one rule remains effective. Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 to the actual calling technology, purpose, and recipient, including applicable written-consent and suppression duties.

Separate a patient's access request under 45 CFR 164.524 from a third-party disclosure authorization under 45 CFR 164.508. Confirm identity, signer authority, requested dates, provider, delivery destination, and the electronic record source before transmission. Patient access generally requires action within 30 days, with one additional 30-day extension accompanied by the required written explanation and completion date. Do not sell automatic low-cost law-firm delivery: the Ciox decision and subsequent HHS guidance limit assumptions about third-party directions and patient-rate charges. Classify each request's route, obtain provider pricing, and escalate disputed charges through counsel instead of repeatedly submitting altered authorizations. Determine HIPAA roles from the actual relationship; a law firm is not automatically a covered entity, and an MSO label does not create a business-associate relationship. When the relationship requires one, execute the appropriate business associate agreement before handling protected information. Retrieve into an access-controlled document store, retain source hashes, and give any approved language-model processor only the necessary material under suitable contractual safeguards. Extract dates, drug identifiers, ICD-10 codes, and page citations as evidence candidates. A human reviewer resolves contradictions, and counsel determines whether those facts satisfy the matter's legal and medical eligibility criteria.

sections.heading: 2. Build a six-module ledger with serialized writes and replay-safe transitions
paragraphs: Use the six reference modules below as one concatenated Python script, in table order. They implement the transactional core, not a public API or a medical-document repository. SQLite is suitable for this small team when the database resides on one local host and every writer follows the same transaction functions. Enable foreign keys, a busy timeout, write-ahead logging, and full synchronous commits; use one connection per worker. Each mutation acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE before checking event identity or balances, so competing workers cannot both spend the same remaining receivable or advance one case from the same state. Database uniqueness independently blocks duplicate claimant identities, service invoices, and bank references. Store amounts as integer cents, never floating-point values. A repeated event with identical content returns without changing balances; reusing its key with different content raises an error. Event recording and business mutations commit together or roll back together. The included concurrency check exercises competing receipt allocations against one invoice. These local guarantees depend on the stated deployment boundary; do not place SQLite on a shared network filesystem or advertise distributed exactly-once delivery. The examples are supplied for execution and review, not reported as tests already run.

Keep three authorities distinct in application code: the authenticated actor, the preserved evidence reference, and the ledger transition. The reference assumes a trusted service adapter has already checked actor permissions and verified evidence references before calling its functions. Never expose those functions directly as unauthenticated endpoints. Intake scoring measures administrative completeness only; it does not predict recoveries or substitute for counsel's assessment. Advance cases through RAW, SIGNED, PROOF, and ACCEPTED using an expected-state comparison, with CLOSED as an explicit terminal alternative. SIGNED requires valid engagement evidence, PROOF requires reviewed source material, and ACCEPTED requires counsel's recorded decision. An invoice instead moves from HELD to BILLED after documented completion of its contractual service milestone. There is no operator escrow: any trust-account activity remains external with the law firm and cannot be posted through these functions. The held state is an administrative billing hold, not custody of claimant money. Revenue credits the MSO revenue account only when the service invoice is released; receipts debit bank cash and credit receivables. Operating payments debit expense and credit cash. Do not derive invoices from accepted-case counts, settle client claims through the ledger, or silently net provider refunds against previously recorded expenses.

Separate cohort attribution from posting month. A February receipt for January services belongs to January's operating cohort but February's bank reconciliation. The cohort view therefore explains earned revenue, operating expense, receivables, and collected cash by service cohort, while the monthly cash view explains actual cash movement. Record only reconciled bank transaction identifiers, namespaced by bank account, and retain the original statement in the protected evidence store. The reference accepts positive service invoices, receipts, and operating payments; it deliberately rejects overpayments rather than inventing a refund mechanism. Route credit notes, refunds, foreign currencies, and partial write-offs to a separately designed accounting integration with reviewed reversing entries before using those features in production. Never edit historical postings: immutable-entry triggers protect the journal, and reconciliation exceptions become assigned work items. For outbound provider requests, use a durable dispatch queue and the provider's idempotency facility when available; where it is absent, require a human check after an uncertain send instead of blindly retrying. The reference makes no external calls inside a transaction. Back up the database and document store under separate access controls, restore them into an isolated environment, and compare journal totals before declaring the recovery exercise complete.

import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager

DDL = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    firm TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (firm, event_key)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cases (
    case_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    firm TEXT NOT NULL,
    person_token TEXT NOT NULL,
    tort TEXT NOT NULL,
    completeness INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (completeness BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('RAW', 'SIGNED', 'PROOF', 'ACCEPTED', 'CLOSED')
    ),
    UNIQUE (firm, person_token, tort)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS invoices (
    invoice_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    firm TEXT NOT NULL,
    cohort TEXT NOT NULL,
    contract_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cents > 0),
    state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('HELD', 'BILLED')),
    UNIQUE (firm, cohort, contract_ref)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries (
    entry_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('REVENUE', 'RECEIPT', 'OPEX')),
    reference TEXT NOT NULL,
    firm TEXT NOT NULL,
    cohort TEXT NOT NULL,
    posted_month TEXT NOT NULL,
    invoice_id TEXT REFERENCES invoices(invoice_id),
    debit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    credit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cents > 0),
    UNIQUE (kind, reference),
    CHECK (
        (kind = 'REVENUE' AND invoice_id IS NOT NULL
         AND debit_account = 'AR' AND credit_account = 'MSO_REVENUE')
        OR
        (kind = 'RECEIPT' AND invoice_id IS NOT NULL
         AND debit_account = 'CASH' AND credit_account = 'AR')
        OR
        (kind = 'OPEX' AND invoice_id IS NULL
         AND debit_account = 'OPERATING_EXPENSE' AND credit_account = 'CASH')
    )
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON entries BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON entries BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS events_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON events BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Event records are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS events_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON events BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Event records are immutable');
END;
"""

def open_ledger(path):
    db = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    db.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
    db.executescript(DDL)
    return db

@contextmanager
def transaction(db):
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        yield
        db.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        if db.in_transaction:
            db.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise

def require_text(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError("A substantive reference is required")

def once(db, firm, event_key, payload, change):
    require_text(firm)
    require_text(event_key)
    encoded = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    with transaction(db):
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE firm=? AND event_key=?",
            (firm, event_key),
        ).fetchone()
        if prior is not None:
            if prior[0] != encoded:
                raise ValueError("Event key was reused with different content")
            return False
        change()
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO events(firm,event_key,payload) VALUES(?,?,?)",
            (firm, event_key, encoded),
        )
    return True

REPORT_DDL = """
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS cohort_reconciliation AS
SELECT firm, cohort,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind='REVENUE' THEN cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind='RECEIPT' THEN cents ELSE 0 END) AS receipts_cents,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind='OPEX' THEN cents ELSE 0 END) AS opex_cents,
       SUM(CASE
           WHEN kind='REVENUE' THEN cents
           WHEN kind='RECEIPT' THEN -cents
           ELSE 0 END) AS receivable_cents,
       SUM(CASE
           WHEN kind='REVENUE' THEN cents
           WHEN kind='OPEX' THEN -cents
           ELSE 0 END) AS profit_cents,
       SUM(CASE
           WHEN kind='RECEIPT' THEN cents
           WHEN kind='OPEX' THEN -cents
           ELSE 0 END) AS operating_cash_cents
FROM entries
GROUP BY firm, cohort;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_cash AS
SELECT firm, posted_month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind='RECEIPT' THEN cents ELSE 0 END) AS receipts_cents,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind='OPEX' THEN cents ELSE 0 END) AS payments_cents,
       SUM(CASE
           WHEN kind='RECEIPT' THEN cents
           WHEN kind='OPEX' THEN -cents
           ELSE 0 END) AS operating_cash_cents
FROM entries
GROUP BY firm, posted_month;
"""

def install_reports(db):
    db.executescript(REPORT_DDL)

def unresolved_invoice_balances(db):
    return db.execute(
        """SELECT i.invoice_id, i.firm, i.cohort,
                  i.cents - COALESCE(SUM(e.cents),0) AS remaining_cents
           FROM invoices AS i
           LEFT JOIN entries AS e
             ON e.invoice_id=i.invoice_id AND e.kind='RECEIPT'
           WHERE i.state='BILLED'
           GROUP BY i.invoice_id, i.firm, i.cohort, i.cents
           HAVING i.cents - COALESCE(SUM(e.cents),0) > 0
           ORDER BY i.cohort, i.invoice_id"""
    ).fetchall()
Cohort profit and posting-month cash cannot be mistaken for each other
Match outstanding invoice balances to statements and investigate every unexplained difference
Module six supplies replay, reconciliation, and competing-receipt regression checks

def qa():
    import os
    import tempfile
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

    db = open_ledger(":memory:")
    install_reports(db)
    months = ["2026-01", "2026-02", "2026-03"]
    for index, month in enumerate(months):
        invoice_id = "invoice-" + month
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "hold-" + month, "hold", invoice_id,
            month, month, "contract-admin", 5875000,
        )
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "release-" + month, "release", invoice_id,
            month, month, "service-evidence-" + month,
        )
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "cost-" + month, "cost", None,
            month, month, "bank-operating:cost-" + month, 3642500,
        )
        receipt_args = (
            db, "firm-a", "current-" + month, "receipt", invoice_id,
            month, month, "bank-operating:current-" + month, 2937500,
        )
        assert bill_action(*receipt_args) is True
        assert bill_action(*receipt_args) is False
        if index < 2:
            bill_action(
                db, "firm-a", "balance-" + month, "receipt", invoice_id,
                month, months[index + 1],
                "bank-operating:balance-" + month, 2937500,
            )

    totals = db.execute(
        """SELECT SUM(revenue_cents),SUM(receipts_cents),SUM(opex_cents),
                  SUM(receivable_cents),SUM(profit_cents),
                  SUM(operating_cash_cents)
           FROM cohort_reconciliation"""
    ).fetchone()
    assert totals == (
        17625000, 14687500, 10927500, 2937500, 6697500, 3760000
    )
    cash = db.execute(
        "SELECT operating_cash_cents FROM monthly_cash ORDER BY posted_month"
    ).fetchall()
    assert cash == [(-705000,), (2232500,), (2232500,)]
    assert unresolved_invoice_balances(db) == [
        ("invoice-2026-03", "firm-a", "2026-03", 2937500)
    ]

    checks = {
        "contact_permission": True,
        "identity_verified": True,
        "exposure_reported": True,
    }
    assert intake(
        db, "firm-a", "intake-one", "case-one", "verified-token-one",
        "counsel-tort-code", checks,
    )
    assert not intake(
        db, "firm-a", "intake-one", "case-one", "verified-token-one",
        "counsel-tort-code", checks,
    )
    for expected, target in [
        ("RAW", "SIGNED"), ("SIGNED", "PROOF"), ("PROOF", "ACCEPTED")
    ]:
        assert advance(
            db, "firm-a", "transition-" + target, "case-one",
            expected, target, "verified-evidence-" + target,
        )

    before = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entries").fetchone()[0]
    try:
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "overpayment", "receipt", "invoice-2026-03",
            "2026-03", "2026-03", "bank-operating:excess", 3000000,
        )
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Overpayment was accepted")
    try:
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "current-2026-03", "receipt", "invoice-2026-03",
            "2026-03", "2026-03", "bank-operating:changed-content", 1,
        )
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Conflicting event replay was accepted")
    try:
        bill_action(
            db, "firm-a", "duplicate-bank-event", "receipt",
            "invoice-2026-03", "2026-03", "2026-03",
            "bank-operating:current-2026-03", 1,
        )
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Duplicate bank reference was accepted")
    assert db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entries").fetchone()[0] == before
    assert db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone() == ("ok",)
    assert db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall() == []
    db.close()

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        path = os.path.join(directory, "ledger.sqlite")
        setup = open_ledger(path)
        bill_action(
            setup, "firm-r", "hold", "hold", "race-invoice",
            "2026-01", "2026-01", "race-contract", 500,
        )
        bill_action(
            setup, "firm-r", "release", "release", "race-invoice",
            "2026-01", "2026-01", "race-service-evidence",
        )
        setup.close()

        def competing_receipt(number):
            worker = open_ledger(path)
            try:
                bill_action(
                    worker, "firm-r", "receipt-" + str(number), "receipt",
                    "race-invoice", "2026-01", "2026-01",
                    "bank-race:transaction-" + str(number), 400,
                )
                return True
            except ValueError:
                return False
            finally:
                worker.close()

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
            results = list(executor.map(competing_receipt, [1, 2]))
        assert sorted(results) == [False, True]
        verified = open_ledger(path)
        assert verified.execute(
            "SELECT SUM(cents) FROM entries WHERE kind='RECEIPT'"
        ).fetchone()[0] == 400
        verified.close()
    print("Reference ledger QA passed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    qa()

sections.heading: 3. Walk three monthly cohorts from acquisition spend to reconciled cash
paragraphs: The Base illustration is an earned-service model with flat monthly administrative revenue of $58,750, not 200 contingent referral fees. The monthly statement of work buys defined staffing capacity, marketing operations, record coordination, and reporting; its price must independently survive jurisdiction-specific review. The conversion waterfall is a capacity assumption used to test delivery, not the contractual unit of compensation. Monthly operating costs are $15,000 media, $10,000 contractor delivery, $5,760 retrieval outlays, $2,500 software and protected storage, and $3,165 other operating overhead. These sum to $36,425, leaving $22,325 owner net profit under the scorecard convention. Twelve identical earned months produce exactly $705,000 revenue, $437,100 costs, and $267,900 profit at 38.0%. Retrieval assumes 320 packages averaging $18 each; this is an illustrative vendor-cost assumption, not a statutory price entitlement. The annual Conservative case separately remains $160,000 revenue and $41,600 profit at 26%; the Scaled case remains $1,250,000 revenue and $625,000 profit at 50%. Do not extrapolate either case from this cohort's conversion rate. The $12,000 to $50,000 startup range funds setup and working capital; capital contributions are neither service revenue nor operating profit.

Assume each service month is completed and invoiced before its first collection, with half collected within that month and half the following month. This negotiated collection convention is deliberately separate from advance deposits, which would require a liability workflow before revenue recognition. Month 1 earns $58,750, collects $29,375, pays $36,425, and consumes $7,050 of working capital. Month 2 collects $29,375 from Month 1 and $29,375 from Month 2, producing $22,325 positive operating cash. Month 3 repeats that pattern. Across the 90 days, earned revenue is $176,250, operating costs are $109,275, accounting profit is $66,975, receipts are $146,875, and cumulative operating cash is $37,600. The $29,375 difference between profit and operating cash is the outstanding Month 3 receivable, collectible in Month 4 under the assumption. Starting with $25,000 available working cash produces month-end balances of $17,950, $40,275, and $62,600 before distributions or separate setup expenditures. Daily timing still matters: a positive month-end balance cannot fund an earlier payment unless the opening balance or actual intervening collections cover it. Maintain a weekly payment calendar alongside this monthly management presentation.

Stress the conversion system without quietly rewriting the canonical Base case. If duplicate and invalid inquiries rise from 20% to 30%, 1,000 raw contacts yield 700 screened contacts, 280 retainers at the same 40% screened conversion, 196 usable proof packets at 70%, and 175 accepted files at the original 200-of-224 acceptance ratio. Retrieval spend falls to $5,040 if only retained matters incur the assumed $18 package cost, but that saving does not repair lost capacity or protect renewal revenue. Independently, a 45% proof-rejection rate on 320 retainers leaves 176 usable packets and approximately 157 accepted files at the same downstream ratio. Report that estimate as a stress result, not an observed cohort count. If 20 additional retrieval packages are required during the 30-day correction window, their $360 incremental cost reduces monthly profit to $21,965 when all other assumptions remain unchanged. Exhausted staffing capacity adds further cost. Pause weak sources, obtain provider quotes, and change scope prospectively rather than billing per accepted case to recover the shortfall. The stated $2,500 to $14,000 monthly operating range is a launch footprint, not the fully loaded Base delivery budget; paid media and scaled service delivery must remain visible.

callout.body: Measure source quality at proof and correction completion, while keeping contract compensation independent of individual claim outcomes.
