sections.heading: 4. Contain privacy-claim pilots, evidentiary failure, and renewal risk
paragraphs: The mapped play cipa_vppa_wiretap_pixel_settlement_arbitrage belongs inside a counsel-led evidence process, not an automated demand factory. For a genuine tracking-related inquiry, preserve the claimant's account of events, the relevant disclosure and consent versions, authorized browser evidence, timestamps, and the actual information allegedly transmitted. Counsel determines applicability, standing, defendant identity, statutory exceptions, limitations periods, and recoverable damages. California Penal Code 631 addresses specified communications interception conduct; it does not make every third-party analytics request an actionable wiretap. The Video Privacy Protection Act, 18 U.S.C. 2710, requires analysis of the statutory provider, consumer, disclosure, and personally identifiable information elements. Do not assume a URL, ordinary page visit, or pseudonymous identifier alone establishes every element. Preserve existing evidence rather than manufacturing plaintiffs, accessing another person's account, or capturing communications beyond the authorized scope. Keep original captures read-only, hash exports, record tool versions, and explain collection limitations. A browser HAR export can contain credentials and sensitive content, so restrict access and produce a reviewed derivative for routine analysis. Retain the original only under the documented preservation and retention policy. Close unsupported matters rather than escalating them to generate administrative volume.

Price the privacy pilot as a distinct administrative research assignment. An illustrative 40 inquiries at $25 screening cost each consume $1,000; eight authorized evidence reconstructions at $75 each add $600. A supported $2,400 fixed service fee therefore leaves $800 contribution before any additional overhead. Counsel might accept three matters, eight matters, or none; the agreed fee remains tied to the completed research scope rather than demands, settlements, or percentages of statutory damages. This pilot is outside the canonical Base cohort and must not be added to its $267,900 annual profit without a separate revised budget. If the evidence fails, the fallback is to close unsupported matters and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits under a new scope. Obtain permission from the relevant site owner before technical testing; claimant authorization alone does not authorize intrusive testing of someone else's systems. An audit can inventory deployed tags, compare observed transmission with disclosures, and verify agreed engineering changes using approved test accounts. Do not condition closing a weak claim on purchasing remediation. Preserve separation between the firm's legal judgment and the MSO's interest in new administrative work, including conflicts arising from serving a prospective opposing party.

Run a weekly exception meeting with four queues: identity and contact authority, provider retrieval, counsel eligibility, and service collections. Give each item an owner, evidence reference, next action, and due date; a dashboard count without a responsible person is not a control. Duplicate clusters trigger source suspension and a preserved vendor dispute file. Medical contradictions trigger human review, never an instruction for the parser to invent missing exposure dates. A material general-causation ruling or Rule 702 expert-evidence exclusion triggers counsel's reassessment of affected campaigns, statements of work, and open intake commitments. Stop incremental acquisition where the approved factual premise has changed, while preserving existing files and communicating through the responsible firm. Collection exceptions trigger invoice-evidence review and contractual follow-up, not movement of client trust funds into the operating account. At day 90, reconcile every accepted file to its evidence trail, every earned invoice to delivered services, and every receipt to a bank transaction. Renew only the capacity that measured proof throughput and payment behavior support. Scaling to two full-time staff and four contractors requires retested queues, coverage, and unit costs; the canonical $625,000 Scaled profit is a separate scenario, not permission to multiply the Base pipeline without examining bottlenecks.

sections.heading: 1. Turn Public Litigation and Product Signals into a Versioned Research Queue
paragraphs: Start with a matter dictionary, not a purchased claimant list. Give each campaign a stable matter identifier, product family, alleged injury vocabulary, exposure dates, responsible attorney, and written intake criteria. The Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation supplies consolidation status and transfer orders; PACER supplies the actual docket and filed documents. CourtListener's RECAP collection is a useful lower-cost discovery layer, but missing documents and delayed uploads make it an incomplete mirror. Record court, docket number, document number, retrieval time, source URL, and a content hash for every instruction-changing order. A clerk-entered scheduling change is different from a lawyer's commentary about that change. Route Rule 702 expert-evidence decisions and changes to plaintiff fact sheets to the supervising firm before changing intake questions. Public availability does not authorize harvesting injured people's identities for unsolicited outreach. Research litigation posture and product evidence; obtain claimant information through an attributable, permissioned interaction. An inexpensive daily docket check can prevent a week of advertising against criteria that the receiving firm has already abandoned. Preserve superseded criteria so later rejection disputes can be reconstructed against the instructions actually active when the inquiry arrived.

Use FDA sources to enrich the matter dictionary, never to manufacture eligibility. The openFDA enforcement endpoint exposes structured recall records, while FAERS supports adverse-event signal research. Neither establishes that a product caused an individual injury, and report counts require attention to duplicate reports, follow-up submissions, reporting changes, and absent exposure denominators. DailyMed contributes label text, ingredient names, dosage forms, and label revision identifiers useful for search normalization. Store the original claimant wording alongside normalized terms; a brand-to-ingredient mapping should not silently become proof of ingestion. Public source refreshes differ from event dates, so carry both the source publication date and the ingestion timestamp. A revised label may arrive after an exposure, and an adverse-event report may describe an event years earlier. Join records by documented identifiers and reviewed mappings rather than fuzzy brand matches alone. For each campaign, maintain a compact evidence packet containing the firm's current criteria, relevant orders, product references, and excluded interpretations. This packet gives media buyers a controlled vocabulary without inviting them to promise recoveries, diagnose injuries, or extrapolate legal causation from a government database entry. Counsel determines which factual claims may appear in each advertisement.

Implement the public-source collector with an allowlisted host registry and a per-source retrieval policy. Python's urllib.request, json, sqlite3, hashlib, and datetime are sufficient for a modest research cache; no browser automation is necessary where an official download or API exists. Store ETag and Last-Modified values when supplied, use conditional requests, and impose request timeouts, response-size ceilings, bounded retries, and jittered exponential backoff. Respect Retry-After and published account quotas rather than assuming that a successful request permits an unlimited crawl. Treat a changed response schema as an exception requiring review, not an invitation to populate blank eligibility fields. Keep a last-success timestamp and visibly distinguish a stale snapshot from a fresh response. PACER spending deserves its own daily cap because repeated docket pulls and large reports can erase the savings from free discovery. Fetch an authoritative document once, retain its permitted internal copy, and reference that copy in subsequent work. The first directory below names six research sources; the next two directories add twelve verification and processing resources. Together they form an eighteen-source stack with explicit access, cost, refresh, and fallback decisions.

sections.heading: 2. Separate Identity Resolution, Provider Discovery, and Patient-Directed Record Access
paragraphs: Build an enrichment waterfall that asks the cheapest relevant question first. Validate contact syntax locally, inspect the originating campaign and permission artifact, then resolve an existing claimant using an internal identifier and limited matching attributes. Use keyed HMAC tokens for normalized sensitive identifiers where deterministic matching is necessary; plain hashes of telephone numbers are vulnerable to enumeration. Send only the minimum required attributes to a contracted identity vendor after confirming the permitted purpose, product terms, and applicable privacy restrictions. A LexisNexis Risk Solutions product can contribute identity signals under its particular agreement; it is not a universal registry of signed retainers. Duplicate representation requires claimant confirmation and a receiving firm's controlled conflict or prior-representation process. Do not circulate identities across unrelated firms to build an informal blacklist. NPPES helps identify provider names, addresses, taxonomy, and identifiers, but an NPI does not establish current licensure or prove treatment. Match the treating facility from claimant-provided information, then confirm the records department through an official channel. This sequencing reserves paid checks for unresolved cases and prevents a weak match from silently excluding a legitimate claimant. Record the reason for every merge and preserve a reversible separation procedure.

Treat medical-record acquisition as several distinct request routes. Under 45 CFR 164.524, an individual generally has access rights to protected health information in a designated record set, subject to specified exceptions. The ordinary federal response period is thirty calendar days, with one permitted thirty-day extension when the required written explanation and completion date are supplied; shorter applicable state requirements may matter. A HIPAA authorization under 45 CFR 164.508 is a different instrument from an individual access request. Following Ciox Health v. Azar and HHS guidance, do not assume that every third-party-directed request receives the individual-access fee limitation or the same mandatory transmission scope. Select the correct route with the firm's documented instructions, identify the requested records precisely, and retain the signed direction and delivery destination. Electronic health-record transmission rights under 42 U.S.C. 17935(e) do not make every provider portal a general-purpose extraction API. Pharmacy records require their own custodian identification and scope, including dispensing dates, drug identifiers, quantities, and reversals where available. Track requests, acknowledgments, invoices, extensions, partial returns, and missing facilities separately. Escalate overdue or misrouted requests through the custodian's published process instead of repeatedly resubmitting duplicate forms.

Normalize returned clinical evidence only after preserving the original files and their provenance. CMS ICD-10-CM releases provide date-sensitive diagnosis vocabulary; they do not transform a billing code into a confirmed injury. Save the code system, release version, encounter date, source page, and surrounding clinical statement. A chronology parser should distinguish patient-reported history, clinician assessment, ruled-out conditions, and copied-forward text. Require source-page citations and human review for exposure and diagnosis assertions that determine acceptance. HealthIT.gov's Certified Health IT Product List helps locate certified products and associated interoperability information, but certification does not grant access to a claimant's chart. FHIR access still depends on the actual provider endpoint, supported implementation, identity workflow, and authorization context. Establish the MSO's role for each engagement rather than assuming every participant is a HIPAA business associate. Where a covered entity or business associate relationship requires one, execute the appropriate agreement and verify that every downstream processing service supports the intended use. Separate public research from protected clinical storage, restrict worker access by matter, and log exports. State bar and Arizona ABS lookups verify professional or entity status; they cannot substitute for analyzing the particular contract and ownership arrangement.

sections.heading: 3. Instrument Permission, Protected Processing, and Vendor Failure Recovery
paragraphs: Create an append-only event ledger spanning raw inquiry, signed law-firm retainer, usable EMR or pharmacy proof, deficiency-free accepted case, and collected MSO or vendor fee. Each event needs a matter identifier, claimant token, timestamp, actor, source artifact, criteria version, and reason code. Keep identity details in a separate restricted store; media dashboards should receive aggregate cohort counts rather than diagnoses or uploaded records. TrustedForm certificates can document aspects of a web interaction, but the certificate is evidence to inspect, not automatic proof that every later call is permitted. Preserve the actual disclosure, named firm, page version, source URL, timestamp, and revocation history. The FCC's 2023 one-to-one consent rule was vacated in Insurance Marketing Coalition v. FCC; do not present it as an operative nationwide mandate. Nevertheless, firm-specific permission is a sensible contractual control, alongside the applicable TCPA rules for the communication technology, state requirements, and advertising restrictions. A Twilio line-type result does not prove ownership, willingness to receive contact, or permission for automated outreach. Reconcile suppression events across intake, dialing, messaging, and vendors before another contact attempt. Keep evidence of the suppression distribution and record failed propagation as an operational incident.

Protected processing requires a different service boundary from marketing analytics. Use a dedicated cloud project or account, least-privilege service identities, encryption, explicit retention schedules, and controlled export destinations. Google Cloud Healthcare API can store supported clinical formats and expose documented interfaces, but it does not retrieve records from arbitrary hospitals. Amazon Textract can produce OCR and structured extraction for supported documents; its output still requires quality checks against the original page. Confirm current service eligibility, executed agreements where required, region, logging behavior, and permitted features before any protected upload. A general-purpose language model should not receive clinical content merely because its interface is convenient. Configure any approved parser to return structured assertions with page references, uncertainty reasons, and explicit abstentions when evidence is absent. Validate dates, drug identifiers, negation, and patient identity before generating a chronology. Documents themselves are untrusted input; embedded instructions must never control the parser's tools or export destinations. Test with synthetic records and approved de-identified fixtures before live use. Measure page-level OCR errors, unsupported assertions, and reviewer corrections, not just processing speed. Preserve the original artifact so a reviewer can resolve a disagreement without rerunning an opaque pipeline.

A small desk needs predictable recovery more than elaborate infrastructure. Use idempotency keys for retrieval orders, certificate claims, invoice creation, and webhook processing. Verify webhook signatures, reject stale replays within a documented tolerance, and retain only the minimum debugging payload. Put failed jobs into a restricted exception queue with an owner and next action. Distinguish authentication failure, quota exhaustion, provider outage, malformed source file, and missing claimant instruction; these require different remedies. Monitor queue age, successful fetch latency, records turnaround, human-review minutes, and collection lag. Cloud request metrics can show technical health while the business quietly accumulates unusable records, so report acceptance outcomes by source and criteria version. Google Search Console supplies delayed organic search performance, not a live ledger of paid conversions. Join its aggregate landing-page signals to first-party campaign reporting without exporting claimant identity. Reconcile vendor invoices against completed jobs weekly and test restore procedures monthly. When a vendor fails, fall back to documented manual custody, secure upload, or deferred processing, not an unapproved consumer service. Every fallback should preserve the same permission, provenance, and deletion requirements as the primary route. Assign a maximum tolerated age to each queue before launch.

sections.heading: 4. Price the Complete Waterfall and Stop Buying When Evidence Economics Break
paragraphs: Apply paid_to_organic_media_arbitrage, the TRACK_2 Paid-to-Organic Media Arbitrage play, to permissioned audience development rather than claimant resale. Test secondary ad networks, vetted newsletter sponsorships, and long-tail search pages against the receiving firm's advertising instructions. The generic play monetizes cheap attention through B2B leads, affiliate payouts, and retained audiences; this volume narrows monetization to contracted administrative and marketing services where the actual arrangement is permitted. Do not import high-ticket affiliate commissions tied to a legal engagement or recovery. Suppose $10,000 buys 5,000 clicks at $2 and produces 1,000 raw inquiries at a twenty-percent submission rate. After two hundred duplicate or invalid inquiries, eight hundred unique inquiries yield two hundred signed law-firm retainers at twenty-five percent. Sixty percent produce usable clinical proof, and eighty percent of those pass the firm's deficiency checklist, leaving ninety-six accepted cases. Media cost is $10 per raw inquiry but approximately $104.17 per accepted case. Neither figure is a permitted fee quote or a recovery forecast. Build an opted-in first-party newsletter around public educational material, not condition-based advertising audiences. Avoid sensitive-health remarketing and vendor uploads that reveal claimant status. Measure retained audience value through attributable service demand.

Reconcile that illustrative monthly cohort to the canonical Base operating envelope. Contracted service revenue averages $58,750 monthly, or $705,000 annually; this is fixed or cost-plus service consideration, not ninety-six contingent case bounties. Allocate $10,000 to media, $6,000 to retrieval at two hundred requests averaging $30, and $20,425 to all remaining labor, software, occupancy, insurance, and operating costs. Total monthly expense is $36,425, leaving $22,325 owner profit. Annual expense is $437,100 and annual owner profit is exactly $267,900, a 38.0% margin. The $30 retrieval assumption is a budgeting average, not a statutory fee entitlement. Revenue allocated across ninety-six accepted packets is about $611.98 each, solely an internal productivity measure. Define service deliverables, replacement periods, documented defects, and remedy caps in the contract without linking compensation to settlements or legal fees. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model professional rule; applicable state enactments and substantive arrangements control. Fixed pricing alone cannot cure impermissible referral payments, interference with professional judgment, or unlawful ownership. Arizona ABS participation requires the relevant authorization, not an address or a generic co-venture label. The law firm retains legal screening and representation decisions.

Stress the waterfall before increasing spend. If duplicate losses rise to thirty percent, the same thousand inquiries leave seven hundred unique prospects and 175 retainers at the existing conversion rate. If usable-proof conversion falls to fifty percent, the cohort produces 87.5 expected proof packets and seventy expected accepted cases after the eighty-percent acceptance step; these are planning expectations, not fractional people in the production ledger. Raising media expense to $12,500 and retrieval to $40 for each of 175 requests produces $7,000 retrieval expense. Holding other expense at $20,425 leaves $18,825 monthly profit on unchanged $58,750 service revenue. This sensitivity is not a replacement scorecard scenario. Replacement labor, contractual credits, or customer attrition would worsen it further. Pause acquisition when duplicate-adjusted accepted-case cost breaches the contracted service budget, usable-proof rates deteriorate, or replacement work consumes reserved capacity. Shift toward first-party newsletter distribution and reviewed organic pages while investigating the vendor. Keep collected fees separate from earned revenue and receivables; delayed payment reduces cash availability without automatically changing recognized revenue. Canonical Conservative and Scaled results remain $41,600 and $625,000 annual owner profit. Settlement awards, trust balances, and client recoveries never enter the MSO revenue denominator.

sections.heading: 1. Assign professional authority before buying claimant traffic
paragraphs: Start with a jurisdiction matrix covering the law firm's offices, each claimant's location, the advertising audience, and the personnel performing intake. ABA Model Rule 5.4 supplies a reference architecture, but the adopted state rule controls; a model rule is not itself a federal statute. Pair the local versions of Rules 5.4, 5.5, 7.2, and 7.3 with runner, barratry, referral-service, and professional-entity restrictions. A fixed price does not sanitize payment for recommending a particular lawyer or improperly soliciting a claimant. The MSO may operate software, schedule appointments, collect factual answers, request records through an authorized route, and prepare source-linked chronologies. The law firm determines eligibility, conflicts, limitations periods, legal strategy, representation, and withdrawal. Its lawyers approve advertising claims and supervise delegated work under applicable professional rules. Contracts must preserve that authority even when the MSO owns the CRM or pays the media invoice. Give the firm an exportable record and the ability to stop communications immediately. Never make access to client information depend on paying a disputed invoice, and never let an intake representative explain expected settlement value as though they were giving the firm's legal opinion.

An Arizona alternative business structure is a separately licensed operating arrangement, not a label that an ordinary marketing company can attach to its agreement. Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31 and ACJA section 7-209 establish the relevant authorization framework; the licensed entity's ownership, management, designated personnel, and ongoing obligations matter. Arizona removed its former ER 5.4 restriction, but that change does not authorize an unlicensed affiliate to practice law or export Arizona permissions into every claimant's state. Evaluate where legal services are delivered, which lawyers are admitted, and which jurisdiction's professional rules apply to each activity. For the ordinary MSO structure used in this scorecard, retain fair-market fixed or documented cost-plus compensation and exclude percentages of legal fees, settlement awards, or case recoveries. Even lawyer-to-lawyer fee divisions require their own applicable conditions; a licensed lawyer's participation does not automatically validate every payment. Document vendor benchmarks, actual staffing, software allocation, media-management work, and pricing assumptions. A $11,750 monthly administrative scope should be explainable through services and capacity rather than a target number of valuable plaintiffs. Review the structure again when ownership, geography, or the service bundle changes.

Use sector-specific stop conditions rather than broad promises that every claimant can be acquired nationally. California Business and Professions Code sections 6151 and 6152 address runners and cappers; Texas Penal Code section 38.12 addresses barratry and related solicitation conduct. Florida's lawyer-advertising rules impose detailed content and filing requirements with exemptions that must be checked against the actual campaign. New York Judiciary Law section 479 restricts solicitation connected with legal business. These provisions differ in elements, exceptions, and covered actors, so a single national script cannot establish permission everywhere. Build routing rules that select an approved state script, authorized firm identity, permissible channel, and current advertising version before contact begins. Treat hospital lists, accident reports, purchased diagnosis lists, and recent-disaster audiences as elevated-risk sources requiring specific examination, not cheap inventory. A vendor's representation that traffic is compliant is supporting evidence, not a substitute for inspecting acquisition methods. Suspend the affected source when its methods cannot be established. Finally, federal Rule of Evidence 702 and MDL causation rulings can eliminate demand without changing the contract's professional boundaries. Maintain a campaign-stop procedure and redeployment plan instead of promising replacements for litigation-wide scientific failures.

sections.heading: 2. Separate patient access, disclosure authorization, and clinical triage
paragraphs: Treat medical-record acquisition as a choice among distinct legal routes. Under 45 CFR 164.524, an individual generally may access protected health information in a designated record set, subject to specified exclusions and procedures. The covered entity generally has thirty days to act, with one permitted thirty-day extension supported by the required written notice. Electronic format depends on what is readily producible or otherwise agreed, not on a vendor's preferred export. A patient-directed electronic transmission request must satisfy the applicable requirements, including clear recipient identification and destination. Following Ciox Health, LLC v. Azar, do not assume the HITECH third-party directive covers every record format or that the individual-access fee limitation applies to every third-party delivery. Distinguish electronic health record requests within the remaining statutory directive from ordinary third-party authorization requests. Under 45 CFR 164.508, a valid authorization must contain its required elements and statements; it does not automatically import the access timetable or fee restrictions. State access laws may provide additional rights or separate fee schedules. Record the selected route, custodian, scope, signature, delivery instruction, and deadline before automation sends anything. Escalate a custodian's disputed interpretation rather than generating repetitive demands under an inapplicable rule.

Determine business-associate status from the actual relationship, not from the presence of health information alone. A plaintiff law firm and its intake vendor are not automatically HIPAA covered entities or business associates merely because a patient authorizes disclosure. Conversely, handling protected information on behalf of a covered entity or another business associate can create obligations that require a compliant agreement under 45 CFR 164.504(e). Map the disclosing entity, recipient, purpose, service, and subcontractor chain before deciding which agreement applies. Regardless of HIPAA status, encrypt stored records, restrict access by matter, log exports, and prohibit model training on claimant material. Evaluate state health-data and breach laws separately; Washington's My Health My Data Act can reach consumer health information outside HIPAA, subject to its scope and exemptions. Identify substance-use-disorder records governed by 42 CFR Part 2 and other specially protected records before using an ordinary authorization. A signature package must reflect the actual disclosure purpose and applicable restrictions. Use secure upload links rather than inviting diagnoses or identifiers in social-media comments. Keep full Social Security numbers out of advertising platforms and routine analytics, and document why any stronger identifier is necessary before collecting it through a restricted channel.

Make the chronology parser an evidence-indexing assistant, not a medical expert or an automated case-acceptance authority. Extract encounter dates, medication names, exposure periods, diagnosis text, ICD-10 codes, and page references while preserving the source document and distinguishing patient reports from clinician findings. An ICD-10 match alone does not establish causation, product exposure, or a viable claim. Require human review of conflicting dates, ambiguous abbreviations, OCR failures, and unsupported model statements. TrustedForm certificates can preserve aspects of a lead-submission event; they do not establish claimant identity, medical eligibility, or the legality of every downstream contact. LexisNexis identity tools require an appropriate product, permissible use, contractual access, and a correction path for false matches. Neither product proves whether another law firm already holds a retainer. Combine restricted identity matching, claimant questions, and counsel-controlled conflict review without creating an unrestricted cross-firm claimant database. For a two-hundred-person retrieval cohort, budget $35 per person as an illustrative blended acquisition outlay, or $7,000 total; this is a procurement assumption, not a statutory fee entitlement. If missing pharmacy periods raise the blended cost to $50, the additional $3,000 must come from an identified reserve or an approved service-scope adjustment.

callout.title: Reduce record friction without overstating legal rights
callout.body: Veteran operators win through route accuracy, traceable evidence, and tightly controlled exceptions.
items: Maintain separate patient-access and third-party-authorization templates; show the selected route on every retrieval ticket so staff do not cite the wrong fee rule.
Request the exact pharmacy date range and product identifiers counsel needs; reconcile dispensing records against exposure narratives before buying another retrieval cycle.
Store TrustedForm evidence with the original disclosure text and form version; a certificate detached from the actual screen cannot explain what the person agreed to.
Attach page-level citations to every chronology assertion and route contradictory dates into a reviewer queue before exporting a lawyer-facing summary.

sections.heading: 3. Price administrative work and contract for defects, not case outcomes
paragraphs: Reconcile every proposal to the supplied Formula v2.0 scorecard before discussing acquisition metrics. Conservative revenue is $160,000 with $118,400 total annual costs, leaving $41,600 at 26%; Base revenue is $705,000 with $437,100 costs, leaving $267,900 at 38.0%; Scaled revenue is $1,250,000 with $625,000 costs, leaving $625,000 at 50%. The respective staffing configurations are one full-time person plus three contractors, one plus three, and two plus four. Illustrative service packaging that exactly matches these revenues is four accounts paying $10,000 quarterly, five accounts paying $11,750 monthly, and ten accounts paying $31,250 quarterly. These are administrative scopes, not purchased inventories of retained plaintiffs. The annual cost totals must absorb the modeled delivery burden rather than silently adding retrieval or media expenses outside the margin calculation. Recognized revenue excludes client trust money, settlement awards, and underlying litigation value. Assess principal-versus-agent treatment under ASC 606 for separately arranged media or retrieval purchases; gross vendor billings do not automatically become operator revenue. No additional retained-share multiplier is supplied for these scenarios. Keep the published service-revenue basis intact and document any pass-through presentation separately rather than inflating the scorecard with client-funded advertising.

Instrument the complete waterfall as raw inquiry -> signed law-firm retainer -> usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof -> deficiency-free accepted case -> collected MSO/vendor fee. The final arrow is a cash-reconciliation link, not a contingent entitlement to payment. For an illustrative monthly cohort, start with 1,000 raw inquiries; quarantine 120 duplicates or suspected synthetic submissions, leaving 880 for permitted contact. If 200 sign retainers, 140 produce usable records, and counsel accepts 120 without administrative deficiencies, the raw-to-accepted yield is 12%. The 60 unusable retrieval files represent a 30% record-stage rejection rate, while 20 additional files fail the final quality review. At $7,000 retrieval outlay, the internal retrieval cost per accepted case is $58.33, but that metric must not become the vendor's compensation formula. Link delivered services to their fixed invoice and collection date even when the accepted count changes. The Base annual cost envelope averages $36,425 monthly; this cohort's retrieval assumption leaves $29,425 for all other modeled costs. A $3,000 retrieval overrun reduces that remaining envelope to $26,425 unless separately funded. Model a 100-case acceptance result and delayed invoice collection as stress conditions, preserving the distinction between operating yield, contracted revenue, and available cash.

Write the master services agreement around deliverables the vendor can control. Scope should identify campaign operations, factual intake, retrieval coordination, chronology preparation, security responsibilities, and explicit exclusions for legal advice and representation decisions. The fee trigger should be a calendar period, documented work, or accepted administrative deliverable, never a retainer signature, settlement, or contingency-fee receipt. Define a thirty-day defect-reporting window as an illustrative negotiated term, with correction or service credits for missing contracted fields, broken evidence links, or unperformed retrieval steps. Do not promise substitute plaintiffs when medical evidence fails or a court changes causation standards. Anti-circumvention language may protect introduced vendor relationships or confidential commercial methods, but must not restrict client choice, lawyer duties, or access to claimant records. Allocate background software and original creative ownership separately from matter information, and require usable exports at termination. Negotiate a liability cap against insurance limits with explicit treatment of confidentiality breaches, intentional misconduct, and indemnity obligations. Specify forum, escalation deadlines, injunctive relief, and transition support. Keep the firm's engagement agreement distinct from the MSO contract so vendor disputes cannot rewrite a claimant's representation terms or delay counsel's protective action.

sections.heading: 4. Deploy original campaigns, evidence-backed consent, and exact scripts
paragraphs: Apply ad_library_spend_velocity_arbitrage to research advertising structure, not to appropriate another firm's identity or creative expression. Inspect Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, and TikTok Creative Center through permitted interfaces at a documented cadence. Record observed first-seen dates, continued activity beyond thirty days, geography, available variants, and changes in quiz architecture. Active duration and expanding variant counts are hypotheses about advertiser commitment, not proof of spend, profitability, or legally supportable claims. Availability differs across platforms, so distinguish directly observed fields from analyst inference. Extract the structural hook, quiz flow, and offer positioning while producing entirely original copy, design, and video assets. Do not copy testimonials, imply government affiliation, or suggest that a compensation fund exists without substantiation. An illustrative $6,000 test generating 300 raw inquiries has a $20 raw cost; if 60 sign, 42 produce usable evidence, and 36 receive counsel acceptance, internal media cost per accepted case is $166.67. These diagnostic ratios do not authorize per-case vendor payment. If identity scrubs remove more inquiries than expected, pause the source and preserve evidence before increasing spend. The fallback is an original campaign built from structural insights, with narrower geography and verified contact permissions, not a copied funnel.

For calls and texts, separate legal requirements from the stricter one-to-one consent policy used by this operation. The FCC's attempted new one-to-one consent restriction was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit in Insurance Marketing Coalition Ltd. v. FCC in January 2025; do not describe that vacated amendment as the operative nationwide rule. Nevertheless, obtain seller-specific permission naming the actual firm as an operational control, especially when lead sellers distribute inquiries. Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 to the actual technology, message purpose, number type, and applicable consent category. Automated dialing, artificial or prerecorded voice, telemarketing, do-not-call rules, and state restrictions require separate analysis; a manually placed call is not a universal exemption. Retain the exact disclosure, affirmative action, timestamp, source URL, form version, and available certificate evidence. Treat consent revocation as a prompt suppression event across relevant systems, following applicable scope and timing rules rather than waiting for a statutory maximum. Apply local calling hours and stricter state requirements through the dialer. Commercial email also needs the applicable CAN-SPAM elements. Before recording a discovery call, apply the relevant state recording-consent rules. Never place medical details in the first voicemail, text preview, or email subject line.

Use verbatim script templates only after substituting the verified firm identity and campaign facts; a script is not evidence that permission exists. For an inbound inquiry, say, 'I handle administrative intake for the law firm named on your request. I am not a lawyer. May I confirm which firm you intended to contact before we discuss your request?' Then resolve any identity mismatch before collecting health details. For discovery, say, 'Have you already signed a representation agreement about this same product and injury? Please tell us the firm name so our supervising lawyer can review the issue; do not cancel an existing agreement based on this call.' For records, explain the actual authorization route and use a secure channel. For uncertain eligibility, say, 'The lawyer will assess the records and applicable criteria. Completing this questionnaire does not establish representation or an expected recovery.' If contact permission is challenged, stop the discussion, suppress further outreach, and investigate the source without asking the person to prove their objection. A quality reviewer should sample recordings where permitted, compare statements against the approved version, and check suppression propagation. Feed confirmed defects back into source suspension, staff coaching, and contract remedies rather than treating high conversion as proof of proper intake.

action_checklist: Build a state-by-state authority matrix covering professional delegation, advertising, solicitation, recording, health information, and contact restrictions.

statutory_citations.relevance: Defines individual-access procedures, response periods, formats, and applicable fee limits; select the correct route before asserting these rights.

statutory_citations.relevance: Supplies required authorization elements and statements for disclosure requests that cannot simply be treated as individual-access requests.

statutory_citations.relevance: Paragraph (e) addresses business-associate contracts when the actual covered-entity service relationship creates that role.

statutory_citations.title: 42 U.S.C. 17935(e) — Electronic health record access
statutory_citations.relevance: Provides the HITECH electronic-record access and transmission foundation, whose third-party implementation must be read with the Ciox decision.

statutory_citations.title: 42 CFR Part 2 — Confidentiality of substance use disorder patient records
statutory_citations.relevance: Requires separate analysis for covered substance-use-disorder records, including consent, redisclosure, and proceeding-related use restrictions.

statutory_citations.title: 47 U.S.C. 227 — Restrictions on telephone equipment
statutory_citations.relevance: Establishes the TCPA framework for covered calls, artificial or prerecorded voice communications, and telephone solicitation restrictions.

statutory_citations.title: 47 CFR 64.1200 — Delivery restrictions
statutory_citations.relevance: Provides operational requirements for covered calls and texts, consent, do-not-call practices, and applicable revocation handling.

statutory_citations.title: 15 U.S.C. 7704 — Requirements for commercial electronic mail
statutory_citations.relevance: Controls applicable commercial-email identification, routing information, opt-out mechanisms, and suppression duties.

statutory_citations.title: California Business and Professions Code section 6152 — Runners and cappers
statutory_citations.relevance: Restricts specified runner and capper conduct; a fixed-fee agreement does not erase prohibited procurement methods.

statutory_citations.title: Texas Penal Code section 38.12 — Barratry and solicitation of professional employment
statutory_citations.relevance: Requires source-method and solicitation review before using targeted claimant outreach or third-party procurement arrangements.

statutory_citations.title: Washington RCW Chapter 19.373 — Washington My Health My Data Act
statutory_citations.relevance: Requires scope and exemption analysis for consumer health information that may fall outside HIPAA-covered processing.

statutory_citations.title: Federal Rule of Evidence 702 — Testimony by expert witnesses
statutory_citations.relevance: Makes scientific admissibility a litigation-demand risk that cannot be cured by promising replacement claimants or expanding administrative screening.

chapters.subtitle: Authenticated Intake, Patient-Directed Record Retrieval, Source-Linked Clinical Chronologies, and Fixed-Fee MSO Distribution
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, ranked #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns repetitive intake and record preparation into a controlled administrative production line. This chapter organizes 13 mapped plays around authenticated webhooks, TrustedForm evidence, permitted LexisNexis identity checks, patient-directed EMR retrieval, and source-linked clinical chronology extraction. Target automation of more than 70% of eligible repetitive labor without delegating representation, medical interpretation, or case acceptance to software. Canonical annual owner profits remain $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. Revenue means contracted MSO service fees, never settlement awards or client trust funds. Distribution compounds through attorney-approved educational assets, voluntary referrals, and measured firm outreach; covert identification of health-related visitors is excluded from the operating design.

sections.heading: 1. Build an authenticated event spine before accelerating intake
paragraphs: Build the operating system around one immutable inquiry identifier, not a spreadsheet row or an advertising platform's conversion count. A Python webhook receiver verifies the provider's supported signature against the original request bytes, checks freshness where supported, records the delivery identifier, and commits the event before acknowledging receipt. A durable queue separates intake from vendor outages; idempotency keys prevent a replay from ordering records twice. Keep clinical documents in an encrypted object store and pass opaque references through the queue. The chapter's 13-play working map comprises consent capture, evidence ingestion, identity reconciliation, fraud triage, retainer handoff, record request orchestration, retrieval recovery, chronology extraction, evidence crosschecking, exception routing, fee reconciliation, referral distribution, and identity_graph_pixel_arbitrage. These are implementation workstreams, not thirteen independently verified businesses. The last play receives a restricted, voluntary-data implementation described below. Assign the full-time operator to queue ownership, vendor management, and billing reconciliation. Assign three contractors to intake exceptions, record retrieval, and clinical abstraction quality checks, with coverage schedules rather than assumed full-time availability. The retained law firm owns engagement decisions, substantive legal screening, and advertising interpretation. Record every handoff with a named owner, deadline, and disposition so automation never becomes an unattended inbox.

Use TrustedForm certificates as evidence of the capture experience, subject to the product's actual retention and access terms; a certificate does not establish identity, case merit, or permission for every downstream use. Store the displayed seller identity, disclosure version, timestamp, source URL, and channel-specific permission alongside the certificate reference. Contract for affirmative permission naming the contacting firm. Do not describe the FCC's vacated 2023 one-to-one lead-generation amendment as an operative federal requirement; apply current TCPA rules, state restrictions, and the actual technology used for calls or messages. For permitted identity verification, procure a suitable LexisNexis product and document its contractual permissible-use restrictions. Avoid collecting full SSNs unless necessary for an authorized workflow. Compare protected identifiers inside a restricted matching service, not inside an advertising account or model prompt. Duplicate retainer detection requires the firm's authorized matter index and claimant confirmation; an identity vendor cannot reveal every existing representation. Similar names, recycled telephone numbers, family addresses, and changed surnames create false matches. Route conflicts to staff for verification and correction, preserving the original evidence. Never automatically reject a person merely because a vendor risk score or incomplete identifier crosses a configurable threshold.

Measure the 70% target against a frozen inventory of repetitive administrative tasks, weighted by observed manual minutes. An illustrative cohort contains 10,000 baseline minutes; 7,300 minutes of work complete without staff touch, while exceptions and required checks consume the remaining 2,700 equivalent baseline minutes. That is 73% touchless coverage, not a claim that lawyers' judgment or all company labor disappears. Track actual review minutes separately because poor extraction can make nominal automation slower than manual work. Count a task as completed only after its required evidence and terminal status exist. A failed vendor request, retried webhook, or draft chronology awaiting verification does not count as success. Start with two weeks of baseline timing and then shadow the automated pipeline against the existing process. Compare duplicate ordering, incorrect record linkage, consent mismatches, and staff minutes per accepted packet. Sample clean outputs randomly as well as inspecting every flagged exception, because confidence filters can hide systematic mistakes. Increase throughput only when measured error rates and queue age remain within written operating limits. The owner should see a daily dashboard of stalled states, aging exceptions, reviewer capacity, and collected service fees rather than a celebratory tally of model calls.

callout.body: The best small-team advantage is a clean evidence trail that makes repeat purchases, disputed permissions, and false identity matches inexpensive to resolve.

sections.heading: 2. Automate retrieval and chronology without manufacturing medical proof
paragraphs: Treat record retrieval as a state machine with distinct legal pathways, not a universal HITECH discount button. Under 45 CFR 164.524, an individual's access request generally requires action within 30 calendar days, with one qualifying extension supported by written notice. Shorter applicable state periods belong in the rules table. Electronic form and format depend on the regulation's readily producible standard and agreed alternatives. Distinguish an individual obtaining their own copy, an applicable patient-directed transmission, and a third-party disclosure supported by an authorization under 45 CFR 164.508. The Ciox decision affected third-party direction and fee treatment; do not automatically impose patient-access fee limits on every attorney-directed request. Store the request route, signature evidence, requested dates, custodian identity, permitted recipient, and response deadline. Pharmacy dispensing history and clinical charts may require different custodians and identity checks. A dispensing event supports a chronology but does not by itself establish ingestion, dosage adherence, exposure duration, or legal causation. Before any PHI-bearing vendor integration, determine the parties' actual roles, execute required business associate agreements, and limit access accordingly. A claimant's permission is not a substitute for contractual safeguards, and a software purchase alone establishes neither authority nor a compliant processing arrangement.

Once a verified document arrives, calculate its digest, preserve the original, and create page-addressable text with extraction quality indicators. Use deterministic parsing for dates, document identifiers, and obvious structured fields before sending limited excerpts to an approved language-model service. Require a strict output schema containing event date, date precision, event type, medication or exposure term, ICD-10 code as documented, source document identifier, page, quoted supporting span, and uncertainty reason. The parser must distinguish diagnosis from rule-out language, encounter dates from historical dates, and documented codes from suggested coding. Never invent a diagnosis code to make a packet appear complete. Validate that every quote exists in the extracted source and that every page reference resolves. Treat embedded instructions inside PDFs as document content, not commands; the extraction worker receives no ability to email records, change billing, or query other matters. Route conflicting medication dates, illegible scans, missing pages, and implausible sequences to the abstraction contractor. The firm receives a source-linked draft, not an autonomous opinion on eligibility. Counsel and qualified specialists retain responsibility for consequential interpretation, including whether the evidence satisfies the firm's current case criteria and whether expert testimony can support causation.

Budget each automated operation using an explicit denominator. An illustrative monthly cohort uses 10,000 lightweight event operations at $0.042 each, or $420, and 1,000 permitted identity checks at $0.60, or $600. These are planning assumptions, not vendor quotations. Add 240 completed retrieval orders at an assumed all-in $22 each, or $5,280; 180 chronology runs at $0.85 each, or $153; and eight review minutes for each chronology at $45 per hour, or $1,080. The resulting variable processing subtotal is $7,533. The chronology run therefore costs $6.85 including this review allocation, before retrieval and acquisition costs. Cap document pages, extracted tokens, and retries per matter; otherwise one corrupt scan can consume the margin from several clean packets. Retry transient transport failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, but send invalid authorization, recipient mismatch, and unsupported format errors directly to staff. After the retry budget expires, create a durable exception with the last provider response and next permitted action. During an extraction outage, continue authenticated intake and manual record indexing while pausing automated chronology publication. Recovery must reconcile already completed work before restarting billable requests, protecting both cash and the claimant's record history.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile the conversion waterfall to contracted service economics
paragraphs: Use the full conversion waterfall as an operating diagnostic, not a disguised contingency fee schedule. An illustrative monthly cohort starts with 1,000 raw inquiries, removes 100 confirmed duplicates and 50 verified invalid submissions, and leaves 850 distinct inquiries for firm-directed screening. Counsel signs 300 retainers. Of 240 completed record retrievals, 180 produce usable HITECH EMR or pharmacy proof; 150 packets become deficiency-free accepted cases. A cohort ledger subsequently associates 135 accepted packets with collected monthly service invoices, while 15 remain associated with unpaid invoices. That final association measures collection coverage, not a price per accepted case. Track the other 60 retained matters awaiting retrieval separately so they cannot vanish from backlog reporting. Record nonqualifying results and administrative deficiencies as different dispositions: a complete chart can demonstrate that a claimant does not meet the firm's criteria. Fees arise from documented fixed monthly services or supported cost-plus work at fair-market rates. ABA Model Rule 5.4 informs the structure, but binding state rules control. Any Arizona ABS arrangement requires actual authorization under that jurisdiction's framework; a contract label cannot create an exception elsewhere. Exclude settlement awards, client trust balances, loan principal, and claimant recoveries from the MSO revenue ledger.

Reconcile the canonical cases before discussing acquisition upside. Conservative revenue of $160,000 less $118,400 of modeled costs produces $41,600 owner profit at 26%. Base revenue of $705,000 less $437,100 produces $267,900 at 38.0%. Scaled revenue of $1,250,000 less $625,000 produces $625,000 at 50%. Staffing remains 1 FT + 3 C for Conservative and Base, then 2 FT + 4 C for Scaled. These figures describe annual contracted MSO services, not underlying litigation value. The Base monthly average is $58,750 revenue, $36,425 total cost, and $22,325 owner profit. Within that illustrative cost envelope, the $7,533 processing subtotal leaves $28,892 for all other modeled expenses, including acquisition, remaining labor, software, overhead, and applicable collection or rework allowances. Do not add that subtotal again when reconciling total cost. Startup capital of $12,000–$50,000 and the stated monthly opex range of $2,500–$14,000 are planning descriptors, not substitutes for the scenario's complete cost envelope. Revenue presentation must reflect the actual principal-versus-agent analysis under ASC 606; pass-through amounts do not become operator revenue simply because cash enters the bank. This supplied scorecard has no separate retained-share multiplier.

Stress the operational assumptions without rewriting the published Base result. Raising average retrieval cost from $22 to $30 on 240 orders adds $1,920 monthly expense. If revenue and other costs remain unchanged, that isolated sensitivity reduces monthly owner profit from $22,325 to $20,405; it is not a replacement scorecard case. Raising the nonqualifying record rate from 25% to 40% reduces usable packets from 180 to 144. Holding the subsequent acceptance ratio at five-sixths produces 120 accepted packets; maintaining 90% collection coverage associates 108 with paid service invoices. Fixed contractual revenue does not automatically fall in that proportion, but replacement work, renewal pressure, and delayed payments can erode economics. Define any replacement window in the service agreement by objective administrative defects, documented notice, and a bounded correction period. An illustrative 30-day correction window is a contract assumption, not a statutory entitlement. Distinguish fixing an omitted page from replacing a case whose scientific theory fails. Maintain a docket-driven pause procedure for material Rule 702 or general-causation rulings, with counsel deciding what changes in screening and advertising. Stop expansion when defect backlog exceeds review capacity, even when traffic remains cheap, because unbounded rework converts a high-margin service into an unsecured working-capital obligation.

callout.body: Expansion requires evidence that the service can accept more work without weakening identity checks, record quality, fee structure, or collection discipline.
items: Verify the firm-specific contact permission, TrustedForm evidence, authorized duplicate check, and unresolved identity queue before releasing a new traffic cohort.

sections.heading: 4. Compound distribution through voluntary participation and reusable evidence
paragraphs: Treat identity_graph_pixel_arbitrage as a proposed distribution hypothesis requiring rejection of its covert health-identification mechanics. Do not resolve anonymous mass-tort visitors into names, home addresses, or disease-linked profiles using CNAME camouflage, bidstream identity feeds, publisher matching tables, or cross-device graphs. A first-party hostname does not transform third-party tracking into an authorized use, and SHA-256 email hashes remain linkable identifiers rather than anonymous information. The proposed 35–55% resolution range is an unverified vendor claim, not a usable forecast. Substitute voluntary identity collection after a clear explanation of the contacting firm, intended channels, and data use. Measure consented engagement rather than deanonymization. For example, 2,000 educational-page visits with a 12% voluntary contact rate produce 240 submissions; 80% permission-and-identity validation leaves 192 contactable inquiries. At $1,200 content and distribution cost, that is $6.25 per contactable inquiry before screening and retrieval. Never cold-email unconsented consumer Gmail addresses from primary domains; moving the same campaign to another domain is not a remedy. US-only edge filtering can support a geographic operating restriction but cannot establish permission, residency, or lawful targeting. Keep sensitive claimant evidence entirely outside advertising audience uploads, even when identifiers are hashed.

Build the programmatic loop from public procedural information and reusable administrative answers, not thin pages promising recovery for every diagnosis. Counsel approves a maintained library covering record-request steps, document preparation, firm contact routes, and accurately dated litigation developments. A publishing script generates accessible pages from approved templates, checks links and revision dates, and stops publication when a controlling source changes. Route medical assertions and legal eligibility language to qualified reviewers before release. Measure voluntary submissions, usable records, and correction workload by page cohort, not search impressions alone. For referral distribution, let readers share a neutral public resource without disclosing their claim status; never auto-invite contacts from a claimant's address book. Illustratively, 200 readers sharing an educational link with 1.5 recipients each generate 300 visits; an 8% voluntary submission rate yields 24 inquiries. If preparation and moderation cost $360, acquisition cost is $15 per inquiry before screening. These are sensitivity inputs, not established conversion rates. Physical mail sits outside CAN-SPAM's commercial email rules, but that does not exempt it from privacy, solicitation, or attorney-advertising restrictions. Limit mailed resources to documented requests or independently justified, reviewed programs, using neutral envelopes that do not disclose a person's suspected condition.

For firm acquisition, maintain a separate business-contact pipeline containing public professional roles, documented outreach sources, suppression status, and service-fit notes. Never enrich that pipeline with claimant medical information. Send individualized messages about administrative capacity, turnaround evidence, and fixed-fee service scope, with the identification and opt-out mechanisms required for commercial email. An illustrative 100 researched firms yield 20 relevant conversations, five paid pilot proposals, and two signed service agreements; $1,800 of research and outreach expense therefore equals $900 per acquired firm, before sales labor omitted from that assumption. Include omitted labor before comparing this channel with paid acquisition. The durable flywheel is operational: reviewed packets reduce deficiencies, documented turnaround supports references, and references lower the cost of acquiring the next appropriate firm. Publish only authorized, aggregated performance summaries with sufficient aggregation to prevent claimant identification. Remove a channel when its downstream rework or permission defects erase its apparent acquisition advantage. If an advertising account is suspended, pause the affected campaigns, preserve evidence, and use the platform's remediation process rather than creating replacement accounts to bypass enforcement. Keep the owned educational library and authorized firm relationships functioning during that pause, so distribution resilience comes from legitimate diversification rather than concealed tracking or platform evasion.

chapters.pull_quote: Automate the movement of evidence, never the invention of proof or the delegation of legal judgment.
action_checklist: Implement authenticated webhook intake with durable event identifiers, idempotent record-order fingerprints, bounded retries, and a named exception owner.
Establish a two-week manual-time baseline and measure touchless completion against eligible repetitive minutes, including separate counts for human review and rework.
Configure route-specific record requests with verified recipients, applicable deadlines, required vendor agreements, and separate tracking for pharmacy and clinical custodians.
Require document digests, page references, supporting quotations, explicit uncertainty, and human verification before any chronology reaches a consequential decision-maker.

Launch voluntary educational, referral, and professional outreach loops with channel-specific unit costs, suppression controls, and no covert identification of health-related visitors.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, ranked #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns 13 mapped plays into a disciplined administrative-services business rather than a wager on settlement proceeds. Start with one full-time operator and three contractors; expand to two full-time seats and four contractors only when measured workload supports the additional capacity. The canonical annual owner profits are $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. Preserve those economics through fixed or cost-plus contracts, duplicate screening, evidence-quality controls, cohort accounting, and collected-cash reconciliation. Cap customer and critical-counterparty concentration at 25%, document contractor IP ownership, and separate administrative acceptance from legal judgment. Buyers pay for replaceable management, assignable contracts, and repeatable earnings; they discount founder dependence, undocumented record access, and settlement-linked compensation.

sections.heading: 1. Assign thirteen plays to four accountable seats before adding capacity
paragraphs: Organize the pod around deliverables, not a miniature law firm. For this chapter, the thirteen-play operating map is an explicit task decomposition: campaign procurement, advertising review coordination, inquiry intake, contact-permission evidence, identity and duplicate screening, law-firm retainer routing, record-request preparation, EMR retrieval, pharmacy retrieval, chronology extraction, deficiency resolution, MSO billing, and buyer-ready reporting. These labels allocate work; they do not establish thirteen separate revenue streams. The full-time operator owns pricing, client relationships, scope control, billing, reporting, and exception escalation. Contractor one owns campaign operations and permission artifacts; contractor two owns intake, identity checks, and retainer routing; contractor three owns record retrieval, chronology production, and administrative deficiency work. Each play receives one accountable seat, one backup, and a documented handoff. The client firm's lawyers retain advertising decisions, representation decisions, legal qualification, and advice. They are counterparties, not hidden employees in the four-person staffing claim. External accounting and security services remain purchased overhead with explicit expense lines. If those services become recurring production labor, revise the staffing disclosure rather than preserving an attractive headcount by relabeling workers. Record weekly hours by play so the claimed automation advantage can actually be measured.

Use written statements of work that price hours or defined administrative deliverables at supportable market rates. An illustrative starting schedule is $45 per hour for campaign operations, $30 for intake administration, and $40 for record operations, each with a separately negotiated monthly hours ceiling. These are budgeting assumptions, not additions to the canonical profit figures. A contractor invoice must identify work period, deliverable IDs, authorized hours, and accepted corrections without exposing medical details in the accounting ledger. Pay for completed administrative work, never a percentage of attorney fees or claimant recovery. Avoid bonuses per signed claimant or accepted legal case; those incentives encourage steering and can implicate referral restrictions even when labeled marketing. Quality incentives should instead reward auditable accuracy, timely handoffs, and reduced operator rework within a fixed services arrangement. Contractor status depends on actual working conditions under applicable tests, not the invoice heading. Define service windows and output standards without pretending that a tightly controlled employee becomes independent through contract language. Require confidentiality, appropriate data-processing terms, and signed IP assignments before access. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a copyright ownership transfer generally requires a signed writing; payment alone does not transfer every script or template.

Scale by splitting bottlenecks rather than duplicating the founder. The second full-time seat becomes delivery and quality lead, while the original operator retains commercial management and cash control. The fourth contractor becomes a dedicated records and pharmacy specialist, allowing the existing records contractor to concentrate on chronology QA and deficiency resolution. That is exactly two full-time seats plus four contractors, not six full-time equivalents. Schedule the expansion only after eight consecutive weeks show sustained utilization above the internally selected 80% planning threshold, acceptable rework, and sufficient contracted contribution to cover the added cost. Maintain a capacity sheet converting volume into minutes for intake, request preparation, follow-up, extraction review, and correction. Automation reduces a measured task duration; it does not erase exception handling. A non-clinical reviewer can check source citations and field completeness but must escalate medical interpretation to appropriately qualified reviewers retained within the disclosed budget. Every production play needs a tested substitute who can resume from the queue without contacting the founder. Test that promise with a five-day operator absence, read-only cash dashboards, and documented escalation authority. If customer service collapses during that exercise, the business still sells the owner's availability rather than transferable operating capacity.

callout.title: Make the founder replaceable before a buyer asks
callout.body: Transferability starts with ordinary production evidence, not a polished sale presentation.
items: Attach each TrustedForm certificate to the exact source event and creative version; a certificate alone does not establish every required calling permission.

sections.heading: 2. Score the complete evidence waterfall without pricing legal outcomes
paragraphs: The weekly scorecard must preserve the entire waterfall: raw inquiry to signed law-firm retainer to usable HITECH EMR or pharmacy proof to deficiency-free accepted case to collected MSO or vendor fee. Tag each event with acquisition cohort, customer, source vendor, matter identifier, timestamp, and responsible seat. A retainer is a law-firm event, not permission for the MSO to practice law; an accepted case means the firm's documented intake standard was satisfied, not that causation or recovery is established. Consider an illustrative monthly cohort of 1,000 inquiries. Exclude 120 duplicates or identity exceptions, route 220 of the remaining 880 into signed retainers, obtain usable proof for 154, and deliver 132 deficiency-free files. Report 25% clean-inquiry-to-retainer conversion, 70% retainer-to-proof yield, and 60% retainer-to-acceptance yield. Record duplicates by reason rather than silently deleting them. A LexisNexis product or another authorized identity service can assist matching, but product permissions, permissible uses, and manual false-positive review remain necessary. Never treat an SSN match or a vendor's exclusive-lead promise as proof that the claimant has no other retainer. Ask the firm to resolve representation conflicts through its own procedures.

Connect that cohort to a services ledger without turning the waterfall into a bounty schedule. The Base scenario averages $58,750 monthly recognized MSO revenue, derived from $705,000 divided by twelve. For a steady-state illustration, allocate that month's service revenue across 132 accepted files: $445.08 per file is an analytical cost-recovery ratio, not a contractual case price. If 90% of the corresponding invoiced amount has been collected by the measurement date, cash receipts are $52,875 and the remaining $5,875 stays receivable subject to collectibility assessment. Do not multiply $445.08 by future cases to rewrite a fixed-fee contract. At an illustrative $45 external retrieval outlay for each of 220 retainers, retrieval spend is $9,900 before internal labor. If non-qualifying evidence rises from 30% to 50%, usable proof falls from 154 to 110. Holding the earlier proof-to-acceptance ratio approximately constant produces about 94 accepted files, raising retrieval outlay per accepted file from $75 to approximately $105.32. The service fee may remain fixed while rework grows; capacity, credits, and renewal economics absorb the shock. Show this stress separately from the unchanged canonical annual scorecard. Repeat the test with duplicate exclusions at 20% and slower provider responses before increasing paid-media commitments.

Define clocks precisely. Intake acknowledgments can target one business day, complete request packets two business days after required documents arrive, and administrative defect correction five business days after a valid notice. These are negotiated MSO targets, not promises that a provider will release records on that schedule. Under 45 CFR section 164.524, covered entities generally have thirty days to act on an access request, with one permitted thirty-day extension subject to the regulation's conditions. Distinguish individual access requests from authorization-based disclosures; patient-rate restrictions and third-party delivery rules do not attach identically to every retrieval route. Track EMR and pharmacy requests separately, including request authority, provider receipt, missing identifiers, lawful charges, and follow-up dates. Use a negotiated thirty-day administrative replacement window measured from delivery, limited to specified vendor-caused defects and documented remedies. A firm's later legal rejection, changed MDL criteria, or Rule 702 causation decision should not automatically create an unlimited replacement obligation. Score first-pass accuracy alongside correction time, and sample high-risk files completely until defects stabilize. Keep medical information out of generic task boards, and use LLM chronology tools only within approved data arrangements, access controls, and human verification workflows.

sections.heading: 3. Protect the canonical margins with accrual books and concentration limits
paragraphs: Keep the Formula v2.0 scorecard intact: Conservative revenue of $160,000 less $118,400 in total modeled costs produces $41,600 owner net profit at 26%; Base revenue of $705,000 less $437,100 produces $267,900 at 38.0%; Scaled revenue of $1,250,000 less $625,000 produces $625,000 at 50%. The first two cases use one full-time seat and three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time seats and four contractors. These are complete annual outcomes, not incremental margins to which an additional labor budget can casually be appended. The listed $2,500 to $14,000 monthly operating range is not a substitute for the complete scenario expense envelope; the case totals also require all modeled delivery and acquisition costs to reconcile. Revenue consists of contracted administrative, marketing, intake, and record-triage services. Client trust balances, settlement awards, claimant damages, and law-firm contingency fees never enter the MSO revenue line. Where the MSO arranges third-party services, assess principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 from the actual control facts. If only a retained service share qualifies as revenue, record that share rather than gross pass-through billings. Do not invent a retained-share percentage or silently alter the canonical figures; identify the accounting difference and reconcile it explicitly for the actual business.

Build the ledger around customer, service period, acquisition cohort, vendor, and delivery activity. Accrue contractor work when performed, record retrieval charges when incurred, and recognize fixed monthly services over the period in which the contractual performance obligation is satisfied. Customer deposits may create contract liabilities rather than immediate revenue. Track credits and bounded replacement obligations using a documented accounting policy that reflects the contract and applicable standards. Maintain separate schedules for invoiced receivables, unbilled amounts, advance collections, disputed invoices, and aging. A cash receipt against last quarter's invoice improves liquidity without increasing this quarter's service revenue. Close monthly within ten business days using bank reconciliations, vendor accruals, cohort cost allocations, and a bridge from operating income to owner distributions. Allocate shared overhead consistently rather than moving unprofitable acquisition costs into an invisible corporate bucket. Reconcile the cohort waterfall to the ledger through service periods and customer identifiers; do not force each accepted file to generate a separate invoice. Preserve both invoice-level detail and an aggregated buyer view stripped of claimant identifiers. A quality-of-earnings review should reproduce monthly margin from source records without requiring unrestricted access to sensitive medical files or the founder's private spreadsheet formulas.

Set concentration limits before a dominant firm or vendor becomes indispensable. Cap each customer group at 25% of trailing-twelve-month recognized revenue and separately at 25% of receivables; aggregate affiliated firms under common economic control. Target five balanced customers so ordinary churn does not immediately breach the ceiling. A simple Base allocation is five customers paying $141,000 annually each, or $11,750 monthly, for an aggregate $705,000. Equivalent illustrative allocations are five annual contracts of $32,000 for Conservative and $250,000 for Scaled, with scope adjusted to the actual labor budget. These are capacity illustrations, not claims that five customers will buy identical packages. For critical acquisition and retrieval counterparties, measure both spend share and routed-volume share, with each economic group capped at 25%. Multiple vendor names do not diversify a common upstream lead supplier. Foundational software needs documented exports and recovery substitutes rather than a fictional four-way split of every application. During initial customer acquisition, disclose any unavoidable concentration breach and make diversification a dated priority; never present an immature book as already diversified. Separately monitor exposure to a single tort thesis because four firms can all lose demand after the same general-causation ruling under Federal Rule of Evidence 702.
