callout.title: Verify four conditions before expanding scope or presenting a sale book
callout.body: Treat unresolved evidence as an operating task with an owner, not as a presentation problem.
items: Verify every MSO agreement uses supportable fixed or cost-plus administrative pricing, preserves lawyer independence, and contains no disguised recovery participation.
Verify the record-request route, disclosure authority, access permissions, and applicable business-associate arrangements before moving medical information into any new tool.
Verify customer revenue, receivables, and critical-vendor routing against the 25% concentration limits, documenting temporary launch-stage breaches and corrective dates.
Verify twelve monthly closes, signed contractor IP transfers, assignment restrictions, and a tested founder-replacement plan before circulating buyer materials.

sections.heading: 4. Value transferable service earnings, not the settlement narrative
paragraphs: A buyer acquires enforceable service economics, documented systems, and an organization capable of continuing without the seller. Owner net profit is therefore the starting point for normalization, not automatically EBITDA or seller's discretionary earnings. Reconcile taxes, interest, depreciation, amortization, owner compensation, recurring replacement labor, and defensible one-time adjustments from actual books. For illustration only, assume the Base $267,900 owner profit contains no owner replacement salary and otherwise requires no EBITDA adjustments. Deduct an $80,000 fully loaded replacement seat to obtain $187,900 normalized annual earnings. A negotiated two-to-three-and-a-half times multiple would imply enterprise value of $375,800 to $657,650. For Scaled, assume $100,000 replacement cost for the remaining owner role, leaving $525,000; a two-and-a-half-to-four times range implies $1,312,500 to $2,100,000. These are illustrative negotiation ranges, not observed transaction comparables or promised clearing prices. The Conservative $41,600 cannot support an $80,000 replacement role on those assumptions, making an owner-operated cash-flow purchase or asset transaction more plausible than a management-independent earnings multiple. If owner labor is already expensed, do not deduct it twice. Support any premium with evidence of renewal durability, stable gross contribution, low rework, and customer continuity through an actual operator transition.

Prepare a transfer package that separates ordinary business assets from restricted information and professional relationships. Include executed customer contracts, service descriptions, renewal history, assignment and change-of-control provisions, vendor agreements, employee documents, contractor statements of work, and signed copyright transfers covering scripts, parsers, templates, and documentation. Inventory third-party and open-source components so the buyer knows which rights can transfer and which require fresh licensing. A contractor's preexisting toolkit needs an express license broad enough for continued operation; an assignment cannot convey rights the contractor never owned. Provide de-identified operating samples initially and stage sensitive disclosures according to the transaction structure and applicable permissions. HIPAA protections and business-associate contract duties do not disappear when an acquisition agreement is signed. Customer contracts may require consent before assignment, and law-firm clients remain free to make representation decisions independently of the MSO sale. Deliver administrator access through controlled account transfers, rotate credentials after closing, and verify exports with a restoration test. The buyer should receive a working service organization, not the seller's personal logins or an unrestricted copy of every claimant record. Keep a transaction issue register with remediation owner, required counterparty action, and evidence of completion.

Negotiate enterprise value separately from equity proceeds. Debt, cash treatment, transaction costs, escrow, working-capital adjustments, and contingent consideration can materially change what the seller receives at closing. Base any earnout on clearly defined MSO service revenue or normalized service earnings, with rules for customer allocation, buyer-imposed overhead, and collection disputes; keep settlement percentages and attorney-fee participation out of the mechanism. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model rule whose binding implementation depends on jurisdiction, so contract review must follow the applicable state rules. Arizona's licensed alternative business structure framework is a specific authorization path, not a portable exception for ordinary MSOs elsewhere. Maintain a one-seller-specific contact-permission policy for campaign operations and separately assess the current TCPA requirements under 47 U.S.C. section 227 and 47 CFR section 64.1200; do not describe the vacated FCC one-to-one lead-generator rule as operative federal law. If offers underprice durable service earnings, retain the business with the same controls: delegated delivery, quarterly concentration testing, documented distributions, and funded correction reserves. A cash cow still requires replacement labor and disciplined renewal work. Sell only when risk-adjusted net proceeds compare favorably with realistic retained distributions and the owner's desired future involvement.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #46, ranked #13 of 49 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, requires a controlled service launch rather than a speculative claimant-buying spree. This sprint organizes 13 mapped plays around one full-time operator and three contractors, from fixed-fee MSO contracting through identity checks, HITECH retrieval, chronology preparation, and invoice collection. Commit no more than $14,000 during the first thirty days against a funded $30,000 launch reserve. Track every inquiry through retained representation, usable proof, firm acceptance, and collected administrative fees without pricing compensation against settlements. The canonical annual owner-profit cases remain $41,600 Conservative, $267,900 Base, and $625,000 Scaled. Day-30, Day-60, and Day-90 decisions depend on mature evidence, cash collection, defect rates, and available pod capacity.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Contract the Service, Fund the Pod, and Define the Evidence
paragraphs: Start with one plaintiff firm, one tort docket, and one documented intake specification. The operating map for Candidate #46 assigns thirteen plays to four people: P1 firm prospecting, P2 fixed-fee MSO contracting, P3 docket and causation monitoring, P4 paid-media acquisition, P5 contact-permission evidence, P6 identity and duplicate screening, P7 scripted intake, P8 attorney retainer routing, P9 electronic medical-record retrieval, P10 pharmacy retrieval, P11 source-linked clinical chronology, P12 deficiency resolution and firm acceptance, and P13 billing and collection. This chapter maps the thirteen operating functions; it does not imply thirteen independent revenue streams. The full-time owner handles P1–P3 and P13. The acquisition contractor handles P4–P5; the intake contractor handles P6–P8; the records contractor handles P9–P12. Client lawyers retain legal judgment and representation decisions outside this administrative pod. Allocate forty owner hours and fifteen hours per contractor weekly, then record actual utilization in Clockify against these play codes. On Day 1, obtain the firm's current exposure criteria, exclusions, representation agreement, and document checklist. On Day 2, establish named decision owners and turnaround targets. Never buy traffic against criteria remembered from an old campaign: changes in product identification, exposure dates, diagnosis requirements, or the litigation record can invalidate otherwise polished intake work.

Days 3 and 4 establish the economic boundary before any claimant information moves. The MSO agreement describes administrative deliverables, staffing, service periods, permitted advertising activity, record-processing responsibilities, and fixed or documented cost-plus charges supported by market comparisons. ABA Model Rule 5.4 is a model, not a nationally operative statute; the firm's supervising lawyer must identify the applicable state rule and any related solicitation restrictions. Do not substitute a per-signed-client acquisition bounty for an expressly prohibited percentage of legal fees. Charges must remain defensible for actual services rather than the sale of recommendations or access to claimants. Reserve settlement negotiations, case valuation, legal screening conclusions, and representation decisions to the firm. Arizona alternative business structure participation requires the relevant license and authorized structure; an Arizona address does not create an exception elsewhere. Define a fifteen-business-day administrative correction window following packet delivery, with dated defect notices and one included correction cycle. That window repairs missing pages, indexing errors, or agreed administrative defects; it does not promise replacement plaintiffs or successful recoveries. Specify invoice dates and dispute procedures independently of settlement events. A collection waterfall may allocate invoice receipts to service cohorts for analysis, but it must not rewrite the underlying compensation arrangement.

Fund a $30,000 launch reserve within the stated $12,000–$50,000 startup range, and authorize at most $14,000 of total Day-1-to-Day-30 cash outflow. Allocate $3,000 to contract and security setup, $3,000 to contractor delivery, $2,000 to media testing, $1,200 to retrieval and indexing, $800 to software, $1,000 to insurance and operating administration, and $3,000 to contingency. These ceilings include deposits and committed purchases; a purchase order consumes available budget before its bank payment clears. During Days 5–7, configure role-based access, multifactor authentication, encrypted storage, audit logs, and the applicable business associate agreements. HIPAA status depends on each party's actual role, not the presence of medical documents alone. Where a covered entity or business associate engages the MSO in that capacity, apply 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e). Use a segregated demonstration workspace with synthetic records before admitting live information. The operator maintains a cash forecast with a $4,000 untouchable operating floor and a weekly commitment review. First deals commonly take one to four months, so Day 30 may legitimately end with qualified proposals rather than revenue. Uncontracted operators stop at demonstrations and prospecting; they do not finance a claimant inventory while waiting for a buyer.

callout.title: Four Checks Before the First Live Inquiry
callout.body: The owner documents these conditions before releasing paid media or receiving live medical records. A failed condition stops the affected activity while the team fixes the specific defect.
items: Confirm an executed fixed-fee or cost-plus scope, applicable state professional-conduct review, and no compensation tied to retainers, legal fees, or settlements.
Confirm the supervising lawyer approved campaign copy, screening scripts, representation routing, and all jurisdiction-specific advertising disclosures.
Confirm role-based access, multifactor authentication, tested deletion controls, and the correct business associate or service-provider agreements for the actual processing relationship.
Confirm funded cash, the $14,000 first-month outflow ceiling, the $4,000 reserve floor, and named owners for all thirteen plays.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Instrument Acquisition Without Buying Fraud or Unauthorized Referrals
paragraphs: Release the first campaign only after the client contract and pre-flight checks are complete. Days 8–10 configure a single landing page, a single named calling firm, and a consent record containing the displayed language, timestamp, source URL, telephone number, and relevant certificate identifier. TrustedForm can preserve evidence of a submitted interaction; it does not prove diagnosis, identity, exposure, or lawful contact by itself. Use one named caller as a contractual risk-control policy, not as a claim that the vacated FCC one-to-one rule remains binding. Apply 47 U.S.C. 227, 47 CFR 64.1200, applicable state calling restrictions, suppression lists, and current revocation requirements to the actual calling technology and campaign. Document state recording requirements before recording calls. The acquisition contractor exports campaign spend daily and maintains a versioned creative register. The intake contractor works only the approved script, identifying administrative criteria without predicting eligibility for compensation. The owner checks ten interactions daily during the first three live days. Suspend any creative that implies guaranteed recovery, firm affiliation that does not exist, or a medical conclusion unsupported by the approved materials. Make source-level spend limits enforceable in the advertising account, rather than relying on a spreadsheet someone remembers to inspect.

Days 11–12 make claimant provenance observable before retainer routing. Create one internal claimant identifier and retain source-specific events so repeat inquiries remain visible without becoming duplicate cases. Compare normalized name, date of birth, telephone, address, and relevant exposure details using restricted access. Do not circulate full Social Security numbers through spreadsheets or advertising systems. Where a LexisNexis identity product is appropriate, verify contractual eligibility, permitted purpose, available coverage, and any applicable consumer-reporting obligations before enabling it. Neither that product nor TrustedForm establishes a universal duplicate-retainer registry. Ask about existing representation and have the client firm resolve potential conflicts or duplicate representation through authorized channels. Classify exact duplicates, probable duplicates, synthetic identities, contact failures, and legitimate repeat submissions separately. Quarantine suspected synthetic submissions rather than automatically accusing people or deleting the audit trail. Establish a source stop at more than 15% confirmed duplicate submissions or more than 3% confirmed synthetic submissions across at least fifty inquiries; a credible coordinated-fraud pattern can justify an earlier pause. Count duplicates against the original purchased denominator so vendors cannot improve reported conversion by removing bad records after billing. Investigate false matches through a second reviewer, and share only the minimum evidence necessary for correction with the source vendor.

Days 13–14 close the first acquisition loop using an explicitly illustrative mature cohort, not a promise that records arrive during week two. Suppose one hundred raw inquiries include ten confirmed duplicates, five synthetic submissions, and five other screening failures, leaving eighty unique screened inquiries. Thirty execute a law-firm retainer after lawyer-controlled routing; twenty-one ultimately produce usable EMR or pharmacy proof; eighteen become deficiency-free accepted cases. The conversion rates are therefore 30% raw-to-retainer, 70% retainer-to-usable-proof, 85.7% proof-to-acceptance, and 18% raw-to-acceptance. A separate $6,000 fixed pilot invoice is collected under its service terms, not earned at a price per accepted claimant. Attribute $1,800 media, $900 delivery labor, $360 retrieval, and $240 allocated software to the cohort: $3,300 direct cost leaves $2,700 contribution before remaining overhead. The analytical cost per accepted packet is $183.33, while allocated collections per accepted packet are $333.33; neither number belongs in a referral-compensation clause. This example's 5% synthetic rate fails the source threshold despite positive contribution. That is the point: profitable-looking invoices cannot excuse contaminated intake. Preserve the rejected records in restricted audit storage under the retention schedule, stop that source, and continue only the separately verified lawful service work.

callout.title: Preserve the Evidence That Vendors Usually Omit
callout.body: Small pods outperform larger intake desks when provenance, denominator discipline, and exception handling are designed before campaign volume increases.
items: Capture the actual landing-page wording alongside the TrustedForm identifier; a certificate without the relevant creative version leaves an avoidable evidence gap.

Request provider-specific encounter ranges and pharmacy dispensing detail, including NDC fields when available, instead of paying repeatedly for broad records that omit the required exposure evidence.
Assign every chronology assertion a source document and page reference; keep model-extracted text distinguishable from the records contractor's verified conclusions.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Retrieve Usable Proof and Measure the Cost of Defects
paragraphs: Days 15–17 open separate EMR and pharmacy request tracks with provider, request type, scope, submission date, acknowledgment, and expected follow-up recorded for each matter. Distinguish an individual's access request under 45 CFR 164.524 from an authorization-based disclosure under 45 CFR 164.508. A signed authorization does not automatically import every access-right deadline or fee limitation. The patient-directed third-party transmission provisions also have limits affected by Ciox litigation; do not apply the patient-rate fee rule universally to attorney-directed retrieval. Confirm the request pathway and current governing requirements before disputing charges. For access requests governed by 164.524, track the thirty-day response requirement and the permitted single thirty-day extension with timely written explanation and a completion date. Set an internal acknowledgment follow-up after five business days without misrepresenting that interval as a statutory deadline. Obtain itemized provider quotes and route any request exceeding $75 to the owner before payment. Seek the needed encounter range, diagnostic material, and dispensing history rather than indiscriminate lifetime charts. Pharmacy records may establish dispensing but not ingestion, causation, or every exposure element. Reconcile patient identity before indexing any returned material, and isolate misdirected records immediately for incident handling under the applicable contract and privacy requirements.

Days 18–19 convert received documents into a source-linked chronology using an approved environment and human verification. The records contractor checks patient identifiers, dates, document completeness, product names, ICD-10-CM codes, prescriber references, and relevant dispensing fields before any packet reaches the firm. A language model can propose event extraction and highlight missing intervals; it cannot establish general causation or replace attorney evaluation. Do not send identifiable records to an unapproved model endpoint. Where business associate duties apply, require the appropriate contractual commitments and security configuration for the processing chain. Mark each extracted assertion with a page reference and distinguish a diagnosis code from the underlying clinical narrative. Sample all initial ten packets, then maintain full checking of identity and material eligibility facts even if routine indexing receives risk-based sampling. Classify resolved record outcomes as usable proof or nonqualifying proof, with specific reasons such as absent diagnosis, incompatible dates, wrong product, or incomplete source material. Keep pending requests in their own aging bucket instead of calling them rejections. For conversion decisions, require at least twenty resolved record matters and separately report the share of all retained matters still pending. A vendor can otherwise manufacture a strong proof rate simply by leaving difficult requests unresolved indefinitely.

Days 20–21 challenge the unit economics before adding another source. In the illustrative cohort, nine of thirty resolved retained matters fail to produce usable proof, a 30% nonqualifying rate. If that rate rises to 50% and acceptance remains approximately 85.7%, thirty retained matters yield roughly thirteen accepted packets instead of eighteen. If retrieval spending also doubles from $360 to $720 and correction labor adds $300, direct cost rises from $3,300 to $3,960. Against the same collected $6,000 fixed invoice, contribution falls from $2,700 to $2,040, or 34%, while analytical cost per accepted packet rises to approximately $304.62. The contract does not automatically increase revenue when documents are difficult. Additional work needs a prospectively agreed service amendment, not a retroactive case bounty. Track defects attributable to MSO processing separately from clinical disqualification and new firm criteria. The fifteen-business-day correction window begins at documented packet delivery, and each notice must identify the missing administrative element. Maintain a PACER docket check and CourtListener alert for material Rule 702 and general-causation developments. An adverse order triggers a lawyer-led campaign reassessment, not an automated declaration that all claimants have lost. Suspend expansion while the firm updates its written acquisition specification and the owner recomputes the cost of remaining work.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Reviews at Days 60/90: Kill the Defect, Fix the Process, Scale Collected Work
paragraphs: During Days 22–26, reconcile campaign spend, contractor time, provider charges, delivered services, invoice amounts, and bank receipts. The full waterfall is raw inquiry to signed law-firm retainer to usable HITECH EMR/pharmacy proof to deficiency-free accepted case to collected MSO/vendor fee. The final arrow represents cohort-level collection attribution, not a requirement that a particular case generate payment. Report earned service revenue, invoiced receivables, and collected cash separately. Under the canonical scorecard, Conservative revenue of $160,000 less $118,400 total modeled costs yields $41,600 owner profit at 26%; Base revenue of $705,000 less $437,100 yields $267,900 at 38.0%; Scaled revenue of $1,250,000 less $625,000 yields $625,000 at 50%. These are operator service amounts, excluding trust funds and settlement awards. No separate retained-share multiplier is supplied, so do not apply an invented haircut. Evaluate gross-versus-net presentation for actual pass-through arrangements under ASC 606 rather than counting client media reimbursements automatically as operator revenue. The $2,500–$14,000 monthly operating range and this sprint's spending cap do not replace the scorecard's total annual cost bases. At later volumes, delivery and acquisition commitments must be funded by collected service revenue and separately authorized budgets. Keep the initial four-person team until measured capacity, rather than optimistic annualization, justifies additional staffing.

Days 27–30 apply conjunctive expansion criteria: every required measure must pass. Day-30 Scale requires one collected pilot invoice, one hundred mature inquiries, twenty resolved record matters, at least ten adjudicated usable-proof packets, raw-to-retainer conversion of at least 25%, proof conversion of at least 65%, acceptance of at least 85%, and collected cohort contribution of at least 35%. Mature inquiries have received the documented contact sequence over at least ten business days or reached a final disposition; packet acceptance excludes packets awaiting firm review, whose aging remains separately visible. Pending record matters cannot exceed 35% of retained matters older than thirty calendar days. Require at least 95% on-time administrative delivery and no more than 80% utilization of the pod's eighty-five weekly available hours. Increase spend by only 20% after a pass. Fix applies to insufficient samples, uncollected pilot invoices, or any missed operating threshold without a hard-stop event; freeze expansion and assign a seven-day corrective test. Kill the affected source or activity for fabricated permission, unresolved material security defects, unlawful compensation, or inability to preserve the $4,000 cash floor. A source exceeding the fraud limits remains paused until independently corrected. Day-30 absence of a deal alone means Fix, not abandonment of a model with a one-to-four-month sales cycle.

Day 60 requires two paid service periods, at least two hundred mature inquiries and forty resolved record matters, a 40% collected contribution margin, and all Day-30 quality thresholds before another 20% spending increase. Day 90 requires three paid periods, three hundred mature inquiries, sixty resolved matters, at least thirty adjudicated usable-proof packets, and 45% collected contribution before authorizing the next capacity plan. These contribution thresholds are pilot controls, not replacements for canonical annual owner margins. At either checkpoint, Fix applies when contribution is 20% or higher but below the required threshold, collection exceeds thirty days, sample sizes are incomplete, or utilization exceeds 80%. Kill the campaign after two corrective tests still produce contribution below 20%, or stop the unfunded launch when the reserve floor would be breached. With $30,000 opening cash and $14,000 maximum outflow each month, cumulative collections must reach at least $2,000 by Day 60 and $16,000 by Day 90 to preserve $4,000, assuming no additional funding. Spending less reduces those collection requirements. If Day 90 brings no executed service agreement, stop paid acquisition and new discretionary commitments; retain only an explicitly funded sales extension through month four. Move toward the canonical two-full-time-plus-four-contractor structure only after paid workload and cash coverage support the added people.
